items.title: Sudan: Transfer War Crimes Suspects to ICC
items.description: Click to expand Image Left to right: Governor of South Kordofan Ahmed Haroun in South Kordofan State, August 23, 2011. © 2011 Reuters; Abdel Rahim Mohammed Hussein. © 2010 غيداء نجم الدين سعيد ابراهيم/Wikipedia; and Omar al-Bashir. © 2009 U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Jesse B. Awalt/Wikipedia (The Hague) – Sudanese authorities should immediately transfer former Interior Minister Ahmed Haroun to the International Criminal Court (ICC) to face charges in The Hague, Human Rights Watch said today. Haroun was recently taken into Sudanese custody and faces ICC war crimes and crimes against humanity charges, committed in Sudan’s Darfur region, in 2003 and 2004. On November 8, 2026, the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) reportedly re-arrested Haroun, interior minister of Sudan in 2007, when an ICC arrest warrant was issued against him. He was arrested one day after he took part in a video podcast interview, his first public appearance since 2019. The armed forces have not officially confirmed Haroun’s whereabouts, but media reported that he is detained in Khartoum state. “For two decades, victims of atrocity crimes in Darfur have witnessed Haroun and others evading justice, leading to impunity-fueled cycles of violence that are claiming more victims every day.” said Liz Evenson, international justice director at Human Rights Watch. “If Sudan’s authorities transferred those sought by the ICC to the court in The Hague, as they are obliged to do, it would send a powerful message to those committing crimes today that they too may find themselves in the dock.” Authorities should also transfer former President Omar al-Bashir—who is believed to be in Sudanese custody in Khartoum state as well—and locate, arrest, and transfer former Defense Minister Abdelrahim M. Hussein. The ICC has also issued arrest warrants for both of them, though there is no information available on Hussein’s location. The ICC issued an arrest warrant against Haroun in 2007, and another against Hussein in 2012, for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity committed in Darfur between 2003 and 2004. During that period, Sudanese government forces and allied militias carried out targeted attacks against civilians on the basis of their ethnicity, including killings, rape, forced displacement from their homes and land, and burning of their villages. In 2009 and 2010, the ICC issued two arrest warrants against al-Bashir for alleged war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide committed in Darfur between 2003 and 2008. Following al-Bashir’s ouster in April 2019, Sudanese authorities held Haroun, al-Bashir, and Hussein in custody for charges not related to atrocities in Darfur but failed to transfer them to the ICC. After fighting erupted between SAF and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on April 15, 2023, the authorities moved al-Bashir to Alia military hospital in Omdurman, Khartoum state, where he reportedly remained under guard, while Haroun left detention amid the collapse of prison security, and under circumstances suggesting coordination with judicial authorities. On September 30, 2026, SAF granted al-Bashir initial approval to travel outside of Sudan for medical treatment. Based on media reports, al-Bashir continues to receive medical care at Alia military hospital and is yet to travel abroad. UN Security Council Resolution 1593, referring the situation in Darfur to the ICC prosecutor, requires the government of Sudan to cooperate with the court even though it is not a party to the Rome Statute, the ICC’s founding treaty. In 2021, the ICC’s Office of the Prosecutor signed a memorandum of understanding with the Sudanese authorities addressing cooperation for arrests. The ICC lacks the ability to enforce its own orders and relies on state cooperation to conduct investigations and make arrests. In January and July, the Office of the Prosecutor reported to the United Nations Security Council on its investigation in Darfur, including its continued engagement with Sudanese authorities. In addition to addressing crimes from July 2002 onward, the Office of the Prosecutor is also investigating crimes committed since April 2023 in Darfur. The prosecutor’s office reported “positive” and “significant” cooperation by Sudanese authorities, and assistance in support of its investigative activities, including deployment of the office’s investigative team to Port Sudan. Nevertheless, Sudan has not fulfilled its obligation to carry out the court’s arrest warrants and transfer the wanted suspects to the Hague. The authorities should provide public information on the whereabouts of all the wanted suspects and take immediate steps to allow their transfer to the court, Human Rights Watch said. The African Union, the members of the Atrocity Prevention and Justice Coalition for Sudan–– particularly the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, and Sierra Leone––as well as the European Union and its member states should directly engage with Sudanese authorities, calling on them to comply with their obligation to fully cooperate with the ICC and to transfer Haroun, al-Bashir, and Hussein to the court’s custody. ICC judges have referred to the Security Council several findings of noncooperation against Sudan and ICC member states in relation to the arrest of ICC suspects. However, the council has never taken steps to enforce these findings. UN member states should urge the Security Council to back the ICC’s mandate in Darfur, including by enforcing the court’s findings of noncooperation on arrests. The ICC prosecutor’s office should use its next biannual report to the council, in January 2027, as an opportunity to raise any concerns related to Sudan’s cooperation on arrests. In 2025, the ICC convicted Ali Muhammad Ali Abd-Al-Rahman (also known as Ali Kosheib), a former leader of Sudan’s “Janjaweed” militias, for war crimes and crimes against humanity in Darfur in 2003 and 2004, and sentenced him to 20 years in prison. Kosheib’s trial was possible after he surrendered himself voluntarily to the ICC’s custody in 2020. “For victims and survivors of crimes in Darfur, Sudanese authorities’ promises of cooperation mean little without concrete action,” Evenson said. “Sudan’s international partners should use every diplomatic tool at their disposal to press for the immediate transfer of all ICC suspects in Sudanese custody and make clear that cooperation with the court is not optional.”

items.title: 2027: Tinubu, Uba Sani face no serious opposition — APC group
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Tinubu-Uba Sani Consolidation Front (TUSCOF) has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu and Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, will overcome opposition challenges and secure victory in the 2027 general elections. The group attributed its optimism to what it described as internal wrangling, weakness and uncertainty within opposition parties, insisting that neither Tinubu nor Uba Sani faces a formidable political challenge ahead of the elections. Chairman of TUSCOF, Mohammed Sada Jalal, stated this while interacting with journalists ahead of the inauguration of the Kaduna State All Progressives Congress, APC, campaign committee. Jalal said Uba Sani’s performance in education, healthcare, infrastructure and human development had strengthened the ruling party’s political standing in Kaduna State. He particularly commended the governor’s efforts to promote political and social cohesion, describing his attempts to bridge longstanding divisions between Kaduna North and Southern Kaduna as one of the administration’s major achievements. Responding to criticisms over the distribution of projects and political appointments, Jalal maintained that the governor had demonstrated fairness in spreading development and government opportunities across the state. He cited road projects in Zone One and the number of government appointees from Zaria as evidence that the administration had not concentrated development or political appointments in any particular area. On insecurity and economic hardship, the TUSCOF chairman acknowledged that persistent attacks on communities and the rising cost of living remained serious concerns that could affect the APC’s electoral fortunes. He, however, argued that the challenges would not be sufficient to deny the ruling party victory in 2027, recalling that similar concerns existed during the 2023 general elections when the APC won the presidential contest. Jalal also blamed Nigeria’s electricity crisis for the difficulties confronting businesses and the wider economy, faulting the outcome of the power sector privatisation undertaken under the administration in which former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar served. On the debate surrounding the 2027 presidential contest and power rotation, he defended Tinubu’s re-election bid, arguing that the South should be allowed to complete its eight-year presidential tenure under the existing political arrangement. He urged northern political leaders to reciprocate the support Tinubu had extended to the region, particularly his role in supporting former President Muhammadu Buhari’s emergence and political leadership. Jalal also called on Kaduna residents to support the President’s second-term ambition, citing federal infrastructure projects in the state, including the Abuja-Kaduna highway and railway projects. The TUSCOF chairman dismissed suggestions that former Kaduna State Governor, Nasir El-Rufai, and his son, Bello El-Rufai, could pose a serious electoral threat to the APC. He specifically predicted that Bello El-Rufai would lose his next election, although he did not provide details to support the prediction. On reported political differences between Uba Sani and his predecessor, Jalal expressed optimism that the disagreement could eventually be resolved, describing political differences as part of the dynamics of democratic competition. Speaking on TUSCOF’s preparations for the 2027 elections, he disclosed that the group had established organisational structures to mobilise support for Tinubu and Uba Sani. According to him, the organisation has a constitution, a bank account and formal registration, while more than 50 patrons and about 60 advisers have also been appointed. He said the group’s structure was modelled after a campaign council, adding that its membership included individuals with experience in previous political campaigns. Jalal, who said he participated in earlier campaign organisations, including the 2023 presidential campaign, expressed confidence that the experience and structures assembled by TUSCOF would strengthen its mobilisation efforts ahead of the 2027 general elections. The post 2027: Tinubu, Uba Sani face no serious opposition — APC group appeared first on Vanguard News .

Rio Tinto SimFer célèbre l’arrivée du Wontanara, son premier navire de transbordement, au port de Morebaya
items.description: Morebaya, République de Guinée – SimFer a célébré l’arrivée de son premier navire de transbordement, le Wontanara, au port de Morebaya, ainsi que le retour en Guinée de sa première promotion de marins stagiaires guinéens. Ce double événement marque une étape importante dans le développement des opérations maritimes de Rio Tinto SimFer, renforçant les infrastructures et les capacités locales nécessaires pour soutenir la montée en puissance de la production et les futures exportations de minerai de fer. Après sa cérémonie de baptême en Chine, le Wontanara a désormais achevé son voyage vers la Guinée, où il a été réceptionné avant sa mise en service. Ce navire est le premier d’une flotte de cinq navires de transbordement spécialement conçus pour jouer un rôle clé dans les opérations de logistique maritime de Rio Tinto SimFer. Cette arrivée marque également une étape importante pour la première promotion de marins stagiaires guinéens, de retour au pays après avoir suivi une formation maritime en Chine. Leur parcours témoigne de l’engagement de Rio Tinto SimFer à développer les compétences locales et à offrir aux Guinéens la possibilité de contribuer aux futures opérations maritimes du projet. L’événement a été célébré au port de Morebaya, en présence de hauts représentants du gouvernement guinéen, de Rio Tinto, de Chinalco, de la Compagnie du TransGuinéen (CTG) et d’autres partenaires industriels. Il a permis de saluer les efforts collectifs ayant contribué à l’arrivée du navire, ainsi que les réalisations des marins guinéens. Elias Scafidas, directeur général des opérations internationales, Minerai de fer de Rio Tinto, a déclaré : « L'arrivée du Wontanara marque une étape importante dans la mise en service des infrastructures maritimes nécessaires à la montée en puissance opérationnelle de SimFer. Je tiens à saluer le travail de nos équipes et de nos partenaires industriels, et à remercier le gouvernement guinéen pour son soutien constant. Ce jalon important revêt également une signification particulière alors que nous accueillons notre première promotion de marins guinéens. Leur réussite reflète notre conviction selon laquelle l'investissement dans des infrastructures de classe mondiale doit aller de pair avec le développement des compétences et des capacités locales, contribuant ainsi à jeter les bases du succès à long terme de Simandou. » Marraine du Wontanara, Nènè Hawa Baldé a affirmé : « En accueillant le navire Wontanara à Morebaya, nous assistons à bien plus que l’arrivée d’un simple navire. Nous voyons là un symbole fort du progrès et de l’ambition la Guinée. Simandou offre aux Guinéens la possibilité de développer leurs compétences, de créer des entreprises et de contribuer à un projet qui aura un impact durable sur l’avenir de notre pays. Je suis fière d'être associée à cette étape majeure, qui témoigne à la fois de l'envergure de ce projet et du potentiel de notre peuple . » Alors que la montée en puissance se poursuit, Rio Tinto SimFer continue de mettre l’accent sur le renforcement de ses capacités maritimes, le développement des compétences locales, tout en veillant à assurer la sécurité, l’efficacité et la fiabilité de ses opérations grâce à un système logistique intégré. Notes aux rédactions SimFer SA est la coentreprise entre le gouvernement de la République de Guinée, Rio Tinto et le consortium CIOH, dirigé par Chinalco. Elle est gérée par Rio Tinto pour le compte des partenaires et exploite la mine de SimFer, située dans les blocs 3 et 4 de Simandou. À propos du navire Wontanara Le navire a été officiellement baptisé lors d’une cérémonie organisée en Chine, en présence de représentants de Rio Tinto SimFer, de Chinalco, de SPSM/COSCO, de Canada Steamship Lines (CSL), de Chengxi Shipbuilding et des partenaires du projet. Néné Hawa Baldé, employée de Rio Tinto SimFer au port et marraine du navire, a baptisé le TSV le Wontanara, ce qui signifie « nous sommes ensemble » en soussou, reflétant ainsi l'esprit de partenariat et de collaboration qui anime ce projet. Une fois mis en service, le Wontanara assurera le transport du minerai de fer depuis le port de Morebaya vers les navires océaniques de grande capacité (OGV) ancrés au large, avant son exportation vers les marchés internationaux. Chaque navire de transbordement (TSV) est conçu pour acheminer plus de 40 000 tonnes de minerai de fer par rotation, offrant une solution sûre et efficace pour transférer de grands volumes de minerai vers les OGV sans qu’ils aient à accoster directement au port. L’article Rio Tinto SimFer célèbre l’arrivée du Wontanara, son premier navire de transbordement, au port de Morebaya est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: 19 of 22 shops inspected at West Hills Mall fail tax compliance checks
items.description: The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) has identified 19 non-compliant businesses out of 22 shops inspected during a tax enforcement exercise within the West Hills Mall enclave in Accra. The exercise uncovered several tax infractions, including failure to register for Value Added Tax (VAT), unauthorised use of self-generated invoices, failure to issue VAT invoices and selective issuance of receipts. Assistant Commissioner in charge of Accra Area Enforcement at the GRA, Joseph Adjeikwei Annan, said only three of the 22 businesses inspected were found to be tax compliant. He explained that while some shops were operating without the required VAT registration, others were generating invoices using their own machines without authorisation from the Authority. Some businesses were also found to be issuing manual receipts instead of approved VAT invoices. Among the businesses cited was Exclusive Signature, for using self-generated invoices without authorisation; Grosvenor, for selectively issuing VAT invoices; and Aromatic Laundry, for operating without the required registration. Others included Maxbuy Ghana Limited, which was found using its own invoices despite being VAT-registered, and Frank Phones, for failing to issue invoices. Sweet Roses was also cited over business records written in Chinese. Mr Annan said the affected businesses had been invited to the GRA offices for further interrogation. He said the Authority had also collected relevant records to support preliminary assessments and possible audits, depending on the nature of the infractions. Regarding Sweet Roses, he said the GRA would use translation software to examine the company’s records and establish its tax compliance status. The business has also been invited for further engagement. Mr Annan said the enforcement exercise would continue beyond December, stressing that tax compliance was a daily responsibility and not an end-of-year activity. He said the Authority was also concerned about businesses that declared their tax liabilities but failed to make the corresponding payments. “GRA will therefore intensify its monitoring to ensure that taxpayers not only filed their returns and made payments but also issued the appropriate invoices whenever customers purchased goods or services,” he added. He urged the media to support the exercise by educating the public on their tax obligations and the Authority’s enforcement activities. Mr Annan cautioned businesses against using ignorance of tax requirements as an excuse for non-compliance, warning that interest and penalties would be imposed where violations were established. He also advised business owners and members of the public to demand identification from persons who approach them claiming to be GRA officials. He warned that some individuals could impersonate tax officers to defraud unsuspecting taxpayers and urged the public to verify the identities of persons undertaking enforcement activities.

items.title: Présidentielle en France : le camp Philippe «favorable à ce que l’Ukraine entre dans l’OTAN»
items.description: « La resistance, le combat de l'Ukraine contre la menace russe renforce notre securite, nous allons donc continuer a aider l'Ukraine et nous serons favorables a ce que l'Ukraine entre dans l'OTAN », a declare ce 18 novembre, depuis l'Albert School, ecole privee du Xe arrondissement de la capitale francaise, l'eurodeputee et porte-parole de la campagne d'edouard Philippe, Nathalie Loiseau, dont l'obsession pour la Russie n'est plus a presenter. « Nous ferons tout, egalement, pour arrimer l'Ukraine au projet europeen, a l'Europe », a-t-elle ajoute. Des propos tenus a l'occasion de la presentation du programme du maire du Havre, transfuge des Republicains a la macronie ou il occupa les fonctions de Premier ministre de 2017 a 2020, candidat a la presidentielle. « C'est de rearmement dont nous avons besoin et pas de desarmement », a estime Nathalie Loiseau assurant que « l'effort de Defense, c'est d'abord l'affaire de tous », et mentionnant « un service national obligatoire ». « Chaque jeune se verra proposer un service national civil ou militaire », a-t-elle poursuivi, afin de « faire nation », avec pour objectif « 250 000 reservistes, autant que de militaires d'active ». Apres 2022, les centristes rejouent la carte de l'Ukraine L'ex-ministre macroniste a egalement evoque une nouvelle loi de programmation militaire « de massification », necessaire selon elle pour avoir « plus de soldats, plus de munitions, plus de drones » et « la modernisation » de la dissuasion nucleaire et precise que « bien evidemment, les interets vitaux de la France ne s'arretent pas strictement a notre Hexagone ». « L'argent du contribuable europeen doit aller a des equipements europeens », a-t-elle au moins defendu, en opposition a la tendance de nombreux membres de l'Union europeenne – et de l'OTAN – qui achetent americain. « Je voudrais denoncer l'espece de fascination malsaine de monsieur Melenchon et de madame Le Pen pour monsieur Poutine », a lâche edouard Philippe. « Cette fascination malsaine m'inquiete profondement pour la securite de notre pays, je ne connais pas de vassalisation heureuse et je ne connais aucune vassalisation heureuse avec des dictateurs », a-t-il ajoute, lui dont le pays a envoye des militaires en Ukraine, soi-disant pour des missions d'entraînement et l'entretien de materiel de guerre. Une presence militaire francaise sur un theâtre d'operations, sans que le Parlement n'ait ete prevenu, contre laquelle s'etait eleve, le 17 novembre, le candidat insoumis appelant a ne pas « devenir cobelligerant en Ukraine » . « Soutenir l'Ukraine, parce que c'est notre interet, n'est a mon avis pas une option », a encore affirme edouard Philippe, pointant du doigt les « appetits de puissances qui s'expriment a l'est et parfois au sud ». Philippe, un candidat entre le « ni-ni » et le « en meme temps » Sur les volets autres que la Defense, et qui concernent plus directement les Francais, l'ancien Premier ministre a predit une « catastrophe » pour les revenus, les pensions et les services publics, a l'aune d'une crise financiere qui « a commence ». Celui qui a debute son parcours politique au Parti socialiste a promis une « reduction massive » de la depense publique et un retour a l'equilibre budgetaire d'ici la fin de son eventuel quinquennat, la suppression des 35 heures ou encore la privatisation de France Travail, ainsi que la limitation du statut de fonctionnaire aux seuls agents des fonctions regaliennes et des enseignants. En termes de retraite, edouard Philippe s'est targue d'avoir dans ses cartons la reforme « la plus ambitieuse du XXIe siecle », qui melerait repartition et capitalisation. Quant a l'immigration, ciblant tour a tour Marine Le Pen et Jean-Luc Melenchon, edouard Philippe a tout d'abord aborde le sujet sous l'angle de la main-d'œuvre. « Nous ne pouvons pas nous en passer », a-t-il assure, renvoyant aux besoins de « nos hopitaux, nos EHPAD, notre secteur agricole, nos restaurateurs », puis exprimant son refus « d'ouvrir grand les vannes de l'immigration, car cela remet en cause notre capacite d'integration », affirmant notamment vouloir « diviser par deux le nombre de titres de sejour ».

items.title: Ex-Spain midfielder Juan Mata retires from professional football at 38
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Spain midfielder Juan Mata has retired from professional football at the age of 38, ending a career that brought international titles and major trophies with Chelsea and Manchester United. Mata, who won 41 caps for Spain, was part of the squad that lifted the 2010 World Cup. Two years later, he helped Spain win Euro 2012, scoring in their 4-0 final victory over Italy. The former Real Madrid youth player joined Valencia in 2007 before moving to Chelsea in August 2011. During his time at Stamford Bridge, he won the Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup. Mata signed for Manchester United in January 2014 and helped the club claim the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup. He left Old Trafford in 2022. He continued his career abroad with Galatasaray in Turkey and Vissel Kobe in Japan, before playing for Australian clubs Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory. Announcing his retirement, Mata said football would remain part of his life. “Football will never leave my life. There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development. “I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer.” The post Ex-Spain midfielder Juan Mata retires from professional football at 38 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: COMMUNIQUÉ DE PRESSE: EQUIP AUTO Côte d’Ivoire 2026 : Le carrefour ouest-africain de la pièce et de la maintenance automobile ouvre grand ses portes aux professionnels burkinabè
items.description: Du 26 au 28 novembre 2026, le Parc des Expositions d’Abidjan accueille la première édition régionale d'EQUIP AUTO en Afrique de l'Ouest. Une opportunité stratégique pour les transporteurs, garagistes, distributeurs et gestionnaires de flottes du Burkina Faso d'accéder sans intermédiaire aux fabricants mondiaux et aux technologies de pointe. Ouagadougou / Abidjan, novembre 2026 — Alors que le secteur des transports au Burkina Faso accélère la modernisation de son parc roulant et de ses corridors logistiques, EQUIP AUTO Côte d’Ivoire s’impose comme l’événement professionnel de référence pour relever les défis de l’après-vente, de la durabilité et de la sécurité routière. Porté par la marque cinquantenaire du salon parisien et soutenu dans la sous-région par la délégation Promosalons, le salon réunira pendant trois jours les plus grands équipementiers, industriels de la rechange, fabricants d’outillages de garage et innovateurs de la mobilité. Pour les opérateurs burkinabè, la tenue de cet événement à Abidjan (espace UEMOA/CEDEAO, sans formalités de visa et partageant le Franc CFA) représente un accès de proximité inédit aux chaînes d'approvisionnement directes. Une opportunité d'affaires concrète : Fabricants en direct et rendez-vous B2B qualifiés Face à la prolifération des pièces de rechange non homologuées et à la complexification des pannes électroniques, EQUIP AUTO Côte d'Ivoire offre aux entrepreneurs et techniciens du Burkina Faso : Un accès direct aux industriels et équipementiers internationaux : contourner les intermédiaires pour négocier des contrats d’importation et d'approvisionnement compétitifs. Un service de rendez-vous B2B sur-mesure : un agenda d'affaires planifié en amont du salon pour rencontrer directement les fournisseurs correspondant aux besoins précis de chaque entreprise (pièces détachées, pneumatiques, lubrifiants, maintenance poids lourds, diagnostic). Au cœur de l’événement : Un Espace Démonstration inédit en conditions réelles L'une des grandes attractions de cette édition 2026 est son Espace Démonstration , conçu comme un véritable atelier grandeur nature. Les professionnels y découvriront : Des tests en direct d’outils de diagnostic de dernière génération (mécatronique, lecture de calculateurs, systèmes ADAS). Des démonstrations pratiques de maintenance sur moteurs thermiques modernes, hybrides et véhicules lourds. Les dernières solutions de levage, de carrosserie-peinture et d'outillage rapide présentées par les formateurs et techniciens d'usine. « Le Burkina Faso est un carrefour stratégique pour le fret et le transit de marchandises en Afrique de l'Ouest. Face aux exigences de rentabilité des flottes et à la modernisation des ateliers, EQUIP AUTO Abidjan est le lieu où les professionnels burkinabè peuvent trouver des solutions immédiates, fiables et directement négociées avec les fabricants, sans les contraintes de coût d'un voyage en Europe. » — La Délégation Promosalons (Sénégal & Burkina Faso) Modalités pratiques et gratuité pour les professionnels Pour encourager une forte participation des acteurs économiques du Burkina Faso, l’accès au salon est entièrement gratuit sur pré-enregistrement : Obtention du badge d’accès gratuit : https://equipauto.mybadgeonline.com/Pro-Login Présentation du salon : Cliquez ici Présentation de la zone expérentielle : CCliquez ici Les organisations professionnelles, coopératives de transporteurs et groupements d'entreprises souhaitant coordonner une venue en délégation peuvent contacter directement le bureau de promotion. items.title: UN WFP pledges month-long food aid for 30,000 displaced in Sudan’s Northern State
items.description: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) has pledged emergency assistance for 30,000 displaced people at El Dabba camp in Sudan’s Northern State for one month, as fresh arrivals from Darfur and Kordofan deepen food shortages and funding cuts threaten further reductions in humanitarian support. The Northern State Humanitarian Aid Commission says it has secured an exceptional allocation from the WFP after food supplies to the camp were interrupted. An estimated 30 displaced families are arriving in El Dabba every day. Cartoon: Omar Dafallah / RD Wail Mohammed Sharif, the state’s humanitarian aid commissioner, says he informed a visiting WFP delegation that food deliveries had stopped. The programme subsequently agreed to provide exceptional assistance for 30,000 people displaced from Darfur and Kordofan for one month. WFP prepares to cut food rations The pledge comes as the WFP warns that funding shortages will force it to reduce food assistance for Sudanese communities facing famine or at risk of it. Ross Smith, the programme’s director of emergency preparedness and response, told journalists in a video briefing that food rations would be cut by 70% from January for communities already facing famine, and by 50% for those at risk of sliding into it. Sharif welcomed the WFP’s intervention, describing it as exceptional support that had not been extended to other Sudanese states or elsewhere in the Middle East. He acknowledged that the programme’s assistance had been affected by funding shortages during November. The state commission is sending urgent appeals to donors to intervene across several humanitarian sectors, he says, warning that some essential services could be disrupted if further support is not secured. Despite the interruption to food supplies, Sharif says the situation remains manageable and that further assistance is expected in the coming days. Displacement continues to rise During a separate meeting with the WFP delegation, led by its Khartoum area manager, El Dabba’s executive director, Mohammed Saber Kishkish, discussed humanitarian needs in the locality and ways to strengthen food assistance for displaced people and new arrivals. Al Hassan Ibrahim Hamed, head of the locality’s emergency and crisis committee, says between 25 and 30 families continue to arrive each day. He stresses the need for sustained food assistance, particularly because displaced people rely on WFP to provide meals. Kawthar Jaafar, the locality’s humanitarian aid commissioner, says the growing number of arrivals from Darfur and Kordofan has created a substantial food gap. Large numbers of new arrivals have been registered in recent days, she says, but available rations are insufficient. She calls for newly displaced families to be given priority in food distributions. The WFP’s Khartoum area manager says the programme continues to coordinate with the government and the humanitarian aid commission. The closure of its office in El Dabba does not mean that assistance has stopped or that the locality’s needs are being ignored, the official says. The programme is also shifting towards support for productive and development projects, alongside food assistance, in an effort to strengthen communities’ ability to become self-reliant. items.title: Every Ghanaian carries a GH¢23,000 share of national debt – Amin Adam
items.description: Former Finance Minister and Ranking Member on Parliament’s finance committee Dr Mohammed Amin Adam has put Ghana’s public debt burden at the equivalent of GH¢23,000 for every citizen, including children, as he questioned the pace of debt accumulation under the current government. Contributing to the debate on the 2027 Budget Statement in Parliament on Thursday, November 19, 2026, the Karaga MP compared debt accumulation under the previous and current administrations. He said the debt stock had increased by US$3.6 billion under the previous period he was discussing, representing an annual average of US$1.8 billion. “In the first two years of President Mahama’s government, they’ve added an annual average of 7.9 billion US dollars,” he stated. Dr Amin Adam said the country’s debt burden, when divided across the population, amounted to about GH¢23,000 per person. “Every Ghanaian today, the 33 million Ghanaians out there, including us in this chamber, we all owe 23,000 Ghanaian cedis. Every Ghanaian, including the children, the Ghanaian child born yesterday, owes 23,000 Ghanaian cedis,” he stated. His figure presents the national debt as an average per-person amount; it does not mean that each Ghanaian has an individual debt. The government has pointed to improvements in macroeconomic indicators, including declining inflation and relative exchange rate stability. The Minority, however, has argued that these improvements are not yet translating into sufficient relief for ordinary Ghanaians. The debate on the 2027 Budget is expected to continue in Parliament.

items.title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
items.description: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph. The 56-year-old New Yorker secured 251 votes in a closed-door, secret ballot, with 11 cast against his nomination, according to US media. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power. His nomination puts him on course to preside over a commanding Democratic majority during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, as his party prepares to reverse Republican policies and investigate the administration. Jeffries must still win a formal vote of the full House when the new Congress convenes on January 3, when he would become the first Black politician to hold the powerful post. With a large Democratic majority, this is seen as something of a formality. Both returning Democrats and incoming lawmakers participated in Wednesday’s election, including progressives who had sought concessions on issues ranging from US military support for Israel to the influence of money in politics. Jeffries had requested a recorded vote rather than a nomination “by acclamation” — without a formal ballot — as some allies had hoped. He argued that every Democrat should have an opportunity to weigh his experience, record and vision, citing the precedent set when the party last took control of the House in 2018. The ballot remained secret, with the overall tally made public but individual votes kept anonymous. Ahead of the election, Jeffries met progressive lawmakers to discuss issues including Israel and healthcare, with proposals to lower the Medicare eligibility age and expand coverage among the topics discussed. The Democratic leader has also sought to shift attention to the party’s plans for governing after voters handed Republicans a crushing defeat amid anger over the Iran war and soaring fuel costs. “Folks are drowning in this Republican economy, and House Democrats are committed to turning that situation around, beginning on day one,” he told reporters Tuesday. “We’re going to relentlessly fight for an affordable America.” – Brooklyn roots – Raised in Brooklyn’s working-class Crown Heights neighborhood, Jeffries trained as a lawyer before entering the New York state legislature in 2007 and winning election to Congress in 2012. Known for his measured manner, sharp rhetoric and penchant for quoting hip-hop artists, he became the first Black politician to lead a party in either chamber of Congress when Democrats chose him to succeed Nancy Pelosi in 2022. He also served as a House prosecutor during Trump’s first impeachment trial in 2020. As speaker, Jeffries would preside over one of Washington’s most powerful institutions and stand second in line to the presidency behind the vice president. But he would face a formidable task in managing a Democratic coalition spanning centrists and an increasingly assertive left flank. His party has promised investigations into Trump and his administration, while lawmakers remain divided over Israel, healthcare and how aggressively to pursue their agenda against a president who retains veto power. Jeffries’s nomination contrasts with a more competitive leadership contest among Senate Democrats, where veteran party chief Chuck Schumer faces a challenge from progressive Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen. Van Hollen has attracted support from prominent left-wing figures, including Bernie Sanders, but acknowledges he is the underdog. Senate Democrats will elect their leader in early December. Republicans chose their own congressional leaders last week, elevating Trump ally Jim Jordan in the House and retaining John Thune in the Senate. items.title: Tinubu’s housing mortgage plan will enslave Nigerians with debt — Gbadamosi
items.description: By Henry Obetta The Lagos State Deputy Governorship Candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Mr. Babatunde O. Gbadamosi, has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s housing mortgage initiative, describing it as an attempt to enslave Nigerians with debt. Gbadamosi, reacting to Tinubu’s announcement of housing financing programmes under the N1 trillion MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund, MREIF, said the proposed monthly repayment of N85,400 was unaffordable to Nigerians earning the national minimum wage of N70,000. The two remarks were made on X, formerly Twitter, yesterday. Tinubu had said eligible Nigerians could access mortgages of up to N100 million at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent, with repayment periods of up to 20 years and an initial deposit of 10 per cent. The President said the initiative was aimed at expanding access to affordable, long-term credit and helping hardworking Nigerians become homeowners. He explained that a prospective homeowner seeking to purchase a N10 million house could make an initial deposit of N1 million and repay approximately N85,400 monthly over 20 years. However, Gbadamosi questioned the affordability of the scheme, arguing that the proposed monthly repayment exceeded the current national minimum wage. “Now, considering that you are alleged to be an accountant, let’s do some accounting, shall we? “The current National Minimum Wage is N70,000. Given that your proposed monthly installment is N85,000 per month, please explain to me like a two-year-old how THIS is any type of affordable housing?” he queried. The ADC chieftain also questioned how retirees approaching the end of their working lives could sustain mortgage repayments for another 20 years, particularly with their pension earnings. “Granted that you seem to be pitching it exclusively to only those who are ‘nearing retirement’, how do you propose they find the N85,000 per month after retirement for twenty years? With their meagre pension?” he asked. Gbadamosi said his party was proposing a different approach to affordable housing in Lagos State, linking housing affordability to improved workers’ earnings. He said he and the ADC governorship candidate in Lagos State, Mr. Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, had promised a comprehensive review of public sector salaries to reflect prevailing economic realities, alongside the provision of at least 100,000 affordable housing units for residents. According to him, the proposed housing units would become affordable through improved salaries. “We have promised a minimum of 100,000 affordable Housing Units to Lagosians. They will be affordable because salaries would have been increased,” he said. Gbadamosi further criticised the Federal Government’s student loan programme, NELFUND, arguing that increased tuition fees had left many students with debts at the beginning of their adult lives. He alleged that the Tinubu administration was introducing debt-based solutions across critical sectors, including education and housing, instead of providing direct social support. “Instead off free education, you brought NELFUND and increased Tuition Fees to a level that the NELFUND cannot cover, thus dumping 1.6 million youths into indebtedness at the start of their adult lives. Now you want to enslave pensioners too?” he said. The ADC deputy governorship candidate accused the President of making life more difficult for Nigerians through his economic policies, insisting that the housing initiative offered little relief to low-income earners. He also vowed that the ADC would work to prevent Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, alleging that the President had manipulated the 2023 election to secure office. Tinubu, in his post, said the mortgage initiative had so far enabled more than 2,300 Nigerians across 27 states to access N160 billion in housing loans through MREIF. He also cited housing loans available through the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria at six per cent interest, with repayment periods of up to 30 years, as well as provisions allowing eligible pension account holders to access up to 25 per cent of their retirement savings towards an initial deposit. The President said the Federal Government was also implementing social housing programmes for vulnerable households, including widows and families of fallen military personnel, while more than 15,000 homes were under construction through the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme. The post Tinubu’s housing mortgage plan will enslave Nigerians with debt — Gbadamosi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: What has Pochettino won as a manager? His record as he joins Man Utd
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United with a career spanning six teams and nearly 700 matches as a manager. The Argentine will be tasked with improving the club’s fortunes after its difficult start to the 2026/27 Premier League season. United appointed Pochettino on Friday to replace Michael Carrick. He is expected to join the club after completing his duties as United States men’s national team coach. Here are key records and achievements from Pochettino’s managerial career: 1. Three trophies with Paris Saint-Germain Pochettino won all three of his major trophies during his time at PSG: the 2020 Trophée des Champions, the 2020-21 Coupe de France and the 2021-22 Ligue 1 title. He joined the French club in January 2021 and worked with high-profile players including Lionel Messi, Neymar and Kylian Mbappé. 2. Took Tottenham to the Champions League final Pochettino led Tottenham to their first UEFA Champions League final in 2019. Spurs lost 2-0 to Liverpool in Madrid. He also guided the north London side to three consecutive top-three Premier League finishes between 2015 and 2018. Tottenham finished second in 2016/17 with 86 points. 3. Southampton’s best Premier League finish at the time Before joining Tottenham, Pochettino took Southampton to eighth place in the 2013/14 Premier League season, matching the club’s best finish in the competition at the time. He was appointed by the Saints in January 2013 after starting his senior managerial career at Espanyol in Spain. 4. Managed 685 matches across six teams Figures published by Transfermarkt show Pochettino has managed 685 matches, winning 337, drawing 146 and losing 202. His overall win rate stands at 49.2 per cent. His six teams have been Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the United States men’s national team. 5. Led the US to the 2026 World Cup round of 16 Pochettino took charge of the United States in September 2024, replacing Gregg Berhalter after the team’s group-stage exit from the Copa América. Under his leadership, the US reached the round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup, recording the country’s most wins at a single edition of the tournament. The Americans also reached the 2025 Gold Cup final. Pochettino now faces the task of improving Manchester United’s fortunes. The club were 18th in the Premier League after taking eight points from their opening 10 matches of the season. The post What has Pochettino won as a manager? His record as he joins Man Utd appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Double scrutin : ELECAM harmonise sa stratégie à Yaoundé
items.description: © DR Les dix délégués régionaux d'Elections Cameroon sont réunis le lundi 17 novembre 2026 à Yaoundé autour du Directeur Général des Elections, Dr Erik Essousse, pour coordonner la préparation des élections législatives et municipales. À moins de trois mois du double scrutin législatif et municipal prévu le 7 février 2027, Elections Cameroon (ELECAM) passe à la vitesse supérieure. Les dix délégués régionaux de l'institution sont réunis le lundi à Yaoundé pour une réunion de coordination stratégique. Placée sous la conduite du Directeur Général des Elections, le Dr Erik Essousse, la rencontre vise à harmoniser les stratégies opérationnelles et à coordonner les actions à mener sur le terrain. Il s'agit, pour l'institution, de parler d'une seule voix et d'assurer une mise en œuvre cohérente du processus électoral sur l'ensemble du territoire national. Au centre des échanges, les défis organisationnels et opérationnels liés à la préparation des prochaines échéances : logistique, déploiement du matériel, formation des personnels, sécurisation des opérations et sensibilisation des électeurs. L'objectif affiché est clair : définir, de concert, les mesures nécessaires pour garantir le bon déroulement des scrutins, dans un cadre inclusif, transparent et impartial. Cette réunion intervient alors qu'ELECAM entend rassurer les acteurs politiques et les citoyens sur sa capacité à organiser des élections crédibles et apaisées. Cet article Double scrutin : ELECAM harmonise sa stratégie à Yaoundé est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Firefighters save 10-room Bimbilla Chief’s Palace compound from fire
items.description: Firefighters from the Bimbilla Municipal Fire Station have contained a fire outbreak at the Bimbilla Chief’s Palace, known as Kpihibara Naa, at Shirkpamo Fong in the Northern Region. The fire affected a two-bedroom apartment within a structure connected to a 10-room compound house, but the swift intervention of the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) prevented the flames from spreading to the remaining rooms. In a Facebook post on Wednesday, November 18, the Service said firefighters successfully contained the blaze, saving all 10 rooms in the compound house from destruction. Although the two-bedroom apartment was affected, the GNFS did not disclose the extent of damage to the property or the cause of the outbreak. The Service commended the firefighters for their timely response and efforts in preventing further destruction. It also urged the public to report fire outbreaks promptly by calling the emergency number 112 and observe fire safety precautions to help prevent similar incidents.

items.title: ‎Tinubu receives state police bill for assent
items.description: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Abuja President Bola Tinubu has received the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, which seeks to establish state police in Nigeria. ‎The bill was formally transmitted to him today by his Special Advisers on Senate and House of Representatives Matters, Senator Basheer Lado and Dr Wasiu Olanrewaju-Smart. ‎This was disclosed via a statement by the Chief of Staff to the PresPolice and Chairman, Presidential Working Group on State Police, Rt. Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila. ‎According to the statement, “All 36 State Houses of Assembly have approved the Bill, exceeding the constitutional requirement of at least 24 States, representing two-thirds of the 36 States, as stipulated in Section 9(2) of the Constitution.” ‎It further stated that President Tinubu will review the Constitution Alteration Bill in consultation with the Attorney-General of the Federation. ‎”He will assent to the bill at a formal signing ceremony,” it added. ‎Meanwhile, Honourable Gbajabiamila, has said that the Presidential Working Group on State Police, which he chairs, with the support of the Policy Advisory Committee, has undertaken extensive stakeholder engagement and nationwide consultations towards developing a draft National Policing Bill. ‎”The draft bill has been submitted to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting validation. Upon receipt of the validated version, the Working Group will review it and present it, alongside its report, to Mr President for consideration,” he said. ‎The former Speaker of the House of Representatives stated, “President Tinubu expresses his appreciation to the President of the Senate, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, members of the National Assembly, the Clerk to the National Assembly, the 36 State Governors, the State Houses of Assembly, and all Nigerians who have demonstrated a shared commitment to addressing the nation’s security challenges.” ‎ ‎ The post ‎Tinubu receives state police bill for assent appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Fire breaks out in top-floor bedroom of Chaka Royal Hotel in North Dayi
items.description: A fire has broken out in a bedroom on the top floor of the three-storey Chaka Royal Hotel at Aveme-Beme in the North Dayi District of the Volta Region, prompting a swift response from the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS). The fire, which occurred on Saturday, November 14, 2026, was extinguished by firefighters from the Anfoega Fire Station, preventing it from spreading to other parts of the hotel. The GNFS said it received a distress call at 0109 hours, following which a team led by Sub-Officer Kwamitse Saviour Yao was immediately dispatched to the scene. Upon arrival, the firefighters observed flames in a bedroom on the top floor of the hotel and swiftly commenced firefighting operations. Through coordinated efforts, the crew managed to bring the fire under control and extinguish it before it could spread to other areas of the building. No casualties were recorded in the incident. In a Facebook post shared on Wednesday, November 18, the GNFS commended the prompt response of its personnel, noting that their swift intervention helped contain the blaze and prevent further damage to the hotel. The Service has, however, urged the public to observe fire safety precautions to minimise the risk of similar incidents. It advised property owners and residents to regularly maintain their electrical installations, avoid overloading electrical sockets and switch off appliances when they are not in use. The GNFS stressed that adherence to these safety measures is essential in preventing electrical-related fire outbreaks and protecting lives and property.

items.title: Moov Africa-ONATEL: la fibre optique double ses débits et casse ses prix jusqu’à 65%
items.description: À compter du 27 novembre 2026, Moov Africa-ONATEL va frapper un grand coup sur le marché de l’Internet fixe au Burkina Faso. L’opérateur annonce le doublement gratuit des débits pour ses abonnés actuels et une réduction pouvant atteindre 65% sur les tarifs de ses offres fibre pour les nouveaux souscripteurs. Une offensive commerciale qui ambitionne de rendre le très haut débit plus accessible aux ménages, aux étudiants et aux acteurs économiques. La fibre optique prend un nouveau virage chez Moov Africa-ONATEL. L’opérateur de télécommunications entend faire tomber davantage les barrières financières et technologiques qui limitent encore l’accès des populations au très haut débit au Burkina Faso. Deux mesures phares sont ainsi annoncées: une augmentation gratuite des débits pouvant aller jusqu’à 100% pour les abonnés actuels et une baisse tarifaire pouvant atteindre 65% pour les nouveaux clients. Ces nouvelles dispositions entreront en vigueur le 27 novembre 2026. Moov Africa-ONATEL annonce le doublement gratuit des débits pour ses abonnés actuels et une réduction pouvant atteindre 65% sur les tarifs de ses offres fibre pour les nouveaux souscripteurs. L’annonce a été faite ce mercredi 18 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou, au cours d’une conférence de presse organisée par Moov Africa-ONATEL. Présentant les nouvelles orientations commerciales de l’entreprise devant les professionnels des médias et des membres de son personnel, Mamadou Idogo, chef du département marketing et communication produit et digital, a relayé le message du Directeur général, Mohamed Karim, absent de la rencontre pour des raisons de calendrier. «À compter du 27 novembre 2026, nous réduirons le prix de la fibre et augmenterons gratuitement les débits de nos clients», a-t-il fait savoir. Derrière cette annonce, l’opérateur affiche une ambition claire: démocratiser l’accès à la connexion Internet à haut débit et permettre au plus grand nombre de profiter des opportunités offertes par le numérique. «Notre ambition est de faire en sorte que la fibre optique ne soit plus un privilège réservé à quelques-uns, mais un service accessible au plus grand nombre. Nous voulons offrir davantage de puissance à nos clients, tout en réduisant considérablement leur effort financier», a souligné Mamadou Idogo. Une double offensive pour les anciens et les nouveaux abonnés La nouvelle politique commerciale repose sur deux leviers complémentaires. Pour les abonnés actuels, la principale innovation est le doublement gratuit des débits, sans augmentation de la facture mensuelle. Concrètement, une formule de 50 Mbps passera à 100 Mbps, tandis qu'un abonnement de 100 Mbps évoluera à 200 Mbps. Une amélioration substantielle qui permettra aux clients de bénéficier d'une connexion plus puissante sans débourser un franc supplémentaire. Des participants à la conférence de presse Autre avantage, cette migration se fera automatiquement et à distance. Les abonnés n'auront donc aucune démarche administrative à entreprendre, aucun déplacement en agence à effectuer et aucun équipement à remplacer, notamment leur box ou leur terminal optique (ONT). Une manière pour l'opérateur de récompenser la fidélité de sa clientèle tout en simplifiant l'expérience utilisateur. Pour les nouveaux souscripteurs, l'effort porte essentiellement sur les prix. Les tarifs des différentes offres fibre connaîtront des réductions pouvant atteindre 65%. Une baisse significative qui vise à lever l'un des principaux obstacles à l'adoption de l'Internet fixe à très haut débit: le coût de l'abonnement. Le cap des 500 Mbps et un réseau de plus en plus étendu Au-delà de la baisse des prix et de l'augmentation des débits, Moov Africa-ONATEL entend également repousser les limites de ses performances commerciales et technologiques. À partir du 27 novembre, l'opérateur proposera une offre pouvant atteindre 500 Mbps. Une capacité qui, selon l'entreprise, constitue une exclusivité sur le marché national des fournisseurs d'accès à Internet. À compter du 27 novembre 2026, Moov Africa-ONATEL va frapper un grand coup sur le marché de l’Internet fixe au Burkina Faso. Cette montée en puissance répond à l'évolution des usages numériques. Télétravail, enseignement à distance, visioconférences, jeux en ligne, streaming, création de contenus et activités professionnelles nécessitent désormais une connexion rapide, stable et capable de supporter plusieurs utilisateurs simultanément. Les ménages comme les entreprises sont ainsi au cœur de cette nouvelle stratégie. Pour soutenir cette ambition, l'entreprise mise également sur la qualité de l'expérience client, avec une attention particulière portée à la stabilité et à la couverture du Wi-Fi ainsi qu'à la réactivité de son assistance technique. Car, au-delà des performances affichées, la fiabilité de la connexion demeure un critère déterminant pour les consommateurs. Un leadership territorial au service de l'inclusion numérique Cette offensive commerciale s'appuie sur un réseau dont l'extension constitue l'un des axes majeurs de développement de Moov Africa-ONATEL. Grâce aux investissements consentis dans le déploiement de la fibre optique jusqu'au domicile, l'opérateur revendique aujourd'hui le maillage territorial le plus étendu du pays, avec une présence dans une quarantaine de localités. Mamadou Idogo, chef du département marketing et communication produit et digital Cette couverture constitue un atout pour rapprocher les services numériques des populations, y compris au-delà des grands centres urbains. L'entreprise entend ainsi accompagner les orientations nationales en matière de transformation digitale et contribuer à faire du numérique un véritable levier de développement économique et social. L'initiative est également présentée comme le résultat d'une démarche d'écoute du marché. Les échanges réguliers avec les associations de consommateurs auraient notamment permis à l'opérateur de mieux cerner les attentes des utilisateurs et d'adapter ses investissements ainsi que sa politique tarifaire aux réalités du terrain. Au-delà de la baisse des prix et de l'augmentation des débits, Moov Africa-ONATEL entend également repousser les limites de ses performances commerciales et technologiques En définitive, avec le doublement gratuit des débits pour ses abonnés actuels, des réductions tarifaires pouvant atteindre 65% pour les nouveaux clients et une offre culminant à 500 Mbps, Moov Africa-ONATEL entend donner un nouveau souffle à la fibre optique au Burkina Faso. Le rendez-vous est désormais fixé au 27 novembre 2026, date à laquelle ces engagements commerciaux entreront en application. Un pari sur l'accessibilité, la performance et l'inclusion numérique, dont les consommateurs seront les premiers juges. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Moov Africa-ONATEL: la fibre optique double ses débits et casse ses prix jusqu’à 65% est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: PROLOG : consolider les acquis et accélérer le développement local
items.description: © DR Le 17 novembre 2026, le Ministre de la Décentralisation a reçu la mission de la Banque mondiale conduite par Mme Chifundo Chilera. Le PROLOG affiche des résultats probants et le Gouvernement en sollicite la prorogation jusqu'en décembre 2028. Le Projet de Gouvernance Locale et de Résilience des Communautés (PROLOG) entre dans une phase décisive. Le Ministre de la Décentralisation et du Développement Local a accordé une audience à la mission de la Banque mondiale, conduite par Mme Chifundo Chilera, pour la restitution de la mission d'appui à la mise en œuvre. Le bilan est encourageant : 95,4 % d'exécution physique pour le premier cycle, près de 500 ouvrages réalisés au bénéfice de 660 450 personnes, et 44,93 milliards FCFA entièrement conventionnés pour le deuxième cycle. Des résultats qui améliorent concrètement les infrastructures de proximité et les conditions de vie des communautés. Pour consolider ces acquis, le Gouvernement sollicite la prorogation du projet jusqu'en décembre 2028, sans financement additionnel. Trois priorités l'accompagnent : renforcer la participation des citoyens, notamment des femmes et des jeunes, assurer la fonctionnalité durable des infrastructures et inscrire les interventions dans la Stratégie nationale de la décentralisation 2026-2035. Le Ministre a réaffirmé l'engagement à accélérer les actions prioritaires : signature des conventions d'allocations de performance, passation des marchés régionaux et lancement des travaux à haute intensité de main-d'œuvre le 20 décembre 2026. Au-delà des ouvrages, le PROLOG veut faire du développement local un moteur de transformation sociale et économique, renforcer la résilience des communautés et promouvoir une décentralisation plus inclusive et plus efficace. L'enjeu est de transformer chaque investissement en bénéfices durables pour les populations. Cet article PROLOG : consolider les acquis et accélérer le développement local est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: OPEC speaks up for fossil fuels at COP31 climate talks
items.description: By William James ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Efforts to boost electrification will depend on fossil fuels, OPEC Secretary General Haitham Al Ghais said on Wednesday at the COP31 talks, where host Turkey is seeking to make increased electricity use a central outcome of the conference. items.title: IAEA chief says planned US-Saudi nuclear deal 'very satisfactory' on inspections
items.description: By Francois Murphy VIENNA, Nov 18 (Reuters) - The provisions in a planned US-Saudi nuclear deal for inspections in Saudi Arabia are "very satisfactory" even though they do not include the gold-standard Additional Protocol, the UN nuclear watchdog's chief said on Wednesday. The proposed deal on civil nuclear cooperation, known as a 123 agreement, has yet to be approved by US lawmakers and has been criticised by nonproliferation experts for not barring Riyadh from enriching uranium or reprocessing spent reactor fuel, two potential ⁠pathways ​to a nuclear weapon.

items.title: Kompany resumes work at Bayern after recovery from illness
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany has resumed work after being hospitalised with meningeal irritation and is expected to return to media duties ahead of Friday’s Bundesliga match against Cologne. According to AFP, the 40-year-old is scheduled to meet the press on Thursday after returning to Bayern’s training ground earlier this week. Vanguard reported that Kompany collapsed while watching a training session on October 23 and was taken to hospital, where he was diagnosed with meningeal irritation. He was later discharged to recover at home, while assistant Aaron Danks led the team during his absence. Kompany was visibly unwell and walked with a limp during Bayern’s 6-1 win over RB Leipzig in mid-October. He was also a doubt for the Champions League match against Arsenal four days later, but took charge of the 2-2 draw before his collapse. His return to the training ground marks a gradual resumption of duties. Bayern have not indicated that he has fully resumed his role, but his scheduled press conference comes ahead of the Cologne fixture on Friday. The post Kompany resumes work at Bayern after recovery from illness appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: «I see you in my dreams»: un hommage poignant aux gardiens de la forêt
items.description: © DR Le Palais des Congrès de Yaoundé a accueilli le 17 novembre 2026, la première du documentaire « I See You in My Dreams », sous le patronage du Ministre des Arts et de la Culture, en présence de la communauté autochtone Baka. Une soirée d'émotion et de mémoire. Le Palais des Congrès a vibré le 17 novembre 2026 au rythme de la première du film documentaire « I See You in My Dreams », organisée sous le patronage du Ministre des Arts et de la Culture du Cameroun, en collaboration avec l'UNESCO, le Haut-Commissariat du Royaume-Uni au Cameroun et le Centre pour l'Environnement et le Développement (CED). Fruit de plusieurs décennies passées aux côtés des peuples autochtones Baka des forêts du Bassin du Congo, le film porte un regard empreint d'humanité sur leurs réalités, leurs aspirations et leurs savoirs. Plus qu'un documentaire sur la forêt, il donne un visage humain à l'un des plus importants patrimoines naturels de la planète. À travers des récits intimes, des visages et des voix trop souvent ignorées, l'œuvre rappelle le rôle essentiel que jouent les peuples autochtones dans la préservation de la forêt. Véritable hommage aux gardiens de la forêt, « I See You in My Dreams » invite chacun à écouter, à découvrir et à renouveler l'engagement collectif en faveur de la protection du patrimoine naturel et culturel pour les générations futures. Cet article «I see you in my dreams»: un hommage poignant aux gardiens de la forêt est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: BoG delays non-interest banking framework rollout for further consultations
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) is delaying the introduction of its proposed non-interest banking framework as it undertakes further consultations and reviews experiences from Kenya and Malaysia. Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Asiama, says the central bank is taking steps to address concerns raised by sections of the public before finalising the framework. Speaking at the 133rd Monetary Policy Committee press briefing, Dr Asiama said a committee established to study the framework had returned from visits to Kenya and Malaysia, where it examined how non-interest banking operates. He said the Bank would meet next week to review the findings and determine the next steps. “We are still working on that framework. Remember, the last time there was some agitation from segments of society, and so we needed to do some additional consulting,” he said. The Governor explained that the committee had been tasked with studying the experiences of the two countries to guide Ghana’s approach to introducing the model. “And so next week we are going to sit and digest the reports from both two countries. But from the initial feedback I’ve got, it’s a framework that is working and working well,” Dr Asiama said. He expressed optimism that Ghana could adopt the framework, describing non-interest banking as an additional player in the country’s financial services industry. The Governor, however, said the Bank would not rush the process to meet a December deadline, stressing the need for thorough consultations and stakeholder buy-in. “It doesn’t have to be necessarily before the end of December. We will make sure everyone is satisfied and convinced that this is something we have to do for the benefit of the nation,” he added. The proposed framework is expected to broaden Ghana’s financial services landscape by providing an alternative banking model for customers.

items.title: Amin Adam accuses government of failing to account for jobs promised in previous budgets
items.description: Ranking member on Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam has accused the government of failing to account for jobs promised under previous budgets, arguing that the 2027 Budget does not adequately address the employment and cost-of-living challenges facing Ghanaians. Contributing to the debate on the 2027 Budget Statement in Parliament on Thursday, November 19, 2026, the Karaga MP said Ghanaians had expected the budget to provide answers to their immediate concerns, particularly joblessness and the rising cost of living. “Unfortunately, Mr Speaker, this budget failed the test. The budget failed the test because it could not account for jobs promised in the 2025 budget and in the 2026 budget,” he stated. Dr Amin Adam cited several employment targets announced in previous budgets, which he said the Finance Minister had failed to account for. He referred to a target of 800,000 jobs under the 2026 Budget, which was presented in November 2025. “The whole 2026 budget was supposed to create 800,000 jobs, announced by the minister when he presented the budget in November 2025. Mr Speaker, the minister failed to give account of a single job that has been created in respect of the 800,000 jobs that he announced in the 2026 budget,” he said. He also questioned progress towards the 24-hour economy programme’s target of creating 1.7 million jobs by the end of 2028. “The budget promised that the 24-hour economy will create 1.7 million jobs by the end of 2028. Again, the minister could not account for a single job,” he stated. The former Finance Minister further cited the Big Push, which he said was expected to create 490,000 jobs, and the Oil Palm Development Programme, with a projected 250,000 jobs. “Mr Speaker, the minister did not account for a single job,” he added. Dr Amin Adam questioned the credibility of the government’s latest employment commitments under its New Economy programme, given what he described as the lack of accountability for previous targets. “If you could not account for the jobs already promised, how do you expect Ghanaians to believe you that the new economy can create additional jobs?” he asked. He argued that the timelines attached to the new programme did not adequately respond to the immediate needs of unemployed young people. “Indeed, if you read the programmes under the new economy, they are promising jobs in 2030, while the Ghanaian people are asking for jobs in 2027. Therefore, the hope it was supposed to restore to the Ghanaian youth who have been searching for jobs, this budget failed to restore that hope,” he said. The 2027 Budget was presented by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson on November 12, 2026. The government has said it will introduce no new taxes and is pursuing a $10 billion New Economy plan as part of its economic agenda. The parliamentary debate on the budget is expected to continue.

items.title: Sudan: Bike-gang-driven crime wave fuels fear in Atbara and Kassala
items.description: Residents of Atbara, in Sudan’s River Nile state, and Kassala in eastern Sudan say gangs known as ‘9 Tawila’ are increasingly targeting people for phone-snatching and theft, while armed robberies have become a growing threat. The gangs use motorcycles to carry out their attacks, which are now taking place in broad daylight, including in markets, main streets and residential neighbourhoods. Residents of Atbara told Radio Dabanga that theft and snatch-and-grab attacks are no longer confined to outlying areas or the hours of darkness. The spread of the incidents into busy public spaces has heightened anxiety among residents. Mustafa Ibrahim, who lives in the El Mamoura neighbourhood, says the activities of the ‘9 Tawila’ gangs have become a daily threat. He cited an incident at a bakery around sunset, when a customer took out his phone to make a bank transfer to pay for his purchases. A thief snatched the phone and fled towards a motorcycle ridden by an accomplice waiting nearby. Ibrahim says he was himself robbed a few days later. He had left an air conditioner on a pick-up truck parked outside his home and went inside to fetch one of his sons to help him carry it. When he returned less than five minutes later, the appliance had disappeared. Surveillance cameras recorded the theft, prompting him to file a police report. He says the thieves now operate at different times of day, apparently undeterred by the risk of being identified. Gunmen on motorcycles in Sudan (Archive photo for illustration) Armed robbery in broad daylight In a more serious incident, Abdel Karim Ahmed told Radio Dabanga that he was the victim of an armed robbery about two weeks ago while travelling alone to the El Wahda neighbourhood in eastern Atbara. Three young men intercepted him at about 10:00 and threatened him with a firearm before taking his phone, money and personal belongings. Ahmed says he later learned of similar attacks in the area. Repeated incidents have made travelling alone through some neighbourhoods increasingly dangerous, particularly as assailants appear increasingly willing to strike during daylight hours. Bashir Abdel Majid, who lives near Atbara market, also told Radio Dabanga that motorcycle thefts and robberies at gunpoint have become major sources of concern among residents. He links the spread of crime to deteriorating economic conditions, rising unemployment and mounting hardship, arguing that these pressures have driven some people to steal and seize other people’s property by force. Abdel Majid questions why the robberies continue despite the heavy deployment of police across the city. Incidents are being reported in different neighbourhoods, he says, without any tangible improvement in residents’ sense of security. Residents are calling on the authorities to increase security patrols to protect people and their property. Armed robbery in Kassala In Kassala, residents say armed robberies have become a daily occurrence. Witnesses told Radio Dabanga that a man was attacked by three people travelling on a motorcycle in Block 6, in North El Halanga, on Monday evening. The group stopped in front of the man in the courtyard of a mosque. One of the assailants attacked him while another brandished a pistol in an attempt to steal his phone. When the man resisted, he was stabbed in the back of the neck. The armed assailant then fired three shots to terrorise residents of the neighbourhood. The attackers managed to take the phone before fleeing. Residents are urging the authorities to intervene urgently, secure the city’s neighbourhoods and bring the armed robberies to an end. items.description: © DR Le Dr Bagayoko Magaran Monzon, Représentant de l'OMS au Cameroun, a reçu le 17 novembre 2026 M. Ukawa Yu, Chef de mission adjoint de l'Ambassade du Japon, pour une rencontre consacrée aux priorités communes en matière de santé publique. L'Organisation mondiale de la Santé (OMS) et le Japon renforcent leur dialogue en faveur des priorités de santé publique au Cameroun. Le Dr Bagayoko Magaran Monzon, Représentant de l'OMS, a reçu M. Ukawa Yu, Chef de mission adjoint de l'Ambassade du Japon au Cameroun, pour des échanges sur les enjeux sanitaires communs. Les discussions ont porté sur la santé maternelle, néonatale et infantile, ainsi que sur la santé sexuelle et reproductive. Les deux parties ont également évoqué la promotion de l'approche « Une seule santé » (One Health), qui intègre les dimensions humaine, animale et environnementale de la santé. Les effets du changement climatique sur la santé et la nécessité d'accélérer les progrès vers l'atteinte des Objectifs de développement durable (ODD) ont aussi été au centre des échanges. Le Gouvernement du Japon et l'Agence japonaise de coopération internationale (JICA) accordent une place importante à la promotion de la sécurité humaine, principe fondamental pour protéger les populations, renforcer leur résilience et soutenir un développement durable. items.title: Santé : le coût des soins du diabète, un défi pour les patients maliens
items.description: Au Mali, le diabete represente un veritable probleme de sante publique. Selon les chiffres officiels, entre 350 000 et 700 000 personnes vivraient avec cette maladie a travers le pays. Au-dela des consequences sur la sante, sa prise en charge constitue un lourd fardeau financier pour de nombreux patients. Entre les depenses medicales, les deplacements et les contraintes alimentaires, le quotidien des personnes concernees reste marque par de nombreuses difficultes. Pour les personnes vivant avec le diabete, la prise en charge ne se limite pas a l'achat des medicaments. Elle implique egalement des consultations regulieres, des examens medicaux, des deplacements vers les structures de sante et une alimentation adaptee. Karfa Maïga, president de la Federation nationale des diabetiques du Mali (FENADIM), souligne l'importance de ces depenses souvent difficiles a supporter pour les patients. « Au-dela des medicaments et des consultations, les personnes vivant avec cette maladie supportent quotidiennement des depenses enormes liees aux deplacements, a l'alimentation adaptee, au suivi medical et aux autres besoins de leur prise en charge », explique-t-il. Le depistage precoce, un enjeu majeur a ces difficultes de prise en charge s'ajoute le defi de la prevention . La sensibilisation et le depistage precoce restent essentiels pour mieux lutter contre la maladie. Moussa Bagayogo, directeur pays de l'ONG Sante Diabete au Mali, invite la population a etre attentive aux signes qui peuvent annoncer l'apparition du diabete. « Des urines frequentes, une perte de poids inexpliquee, une fatigue persistante ou une vision trouble peuvent etre les premiers symptomes du diabete. Il est essentiel de ne pas les ignorer », alerte-t-il. Face a cette situation, les acteurs de la lutte contre le diabete rappellent qu'en plus du depistage precoce et l'information, la lutte contre le diabete passe par un acces plus abordable aux soins. Lire aussi : Diabete : « les femmes plus exposees au Mali » L’article Santé : le coût des soins du diabète, un défi pour les patients maliens est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: BoG says early bondholder repayments will not disrupt liquidity management
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) says it is prepared to manage the liquidity impact of early repayments to domestic bondholders, following concerns about the potential implications for the financial market. Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Asiama, says the central bank was aware of the arrangements under the government’s sinking fund and had anticipated the impact of the repayments on liquidity conditions. Speaking at the 137th Monetary Policy Committee press briefing, Dr Asiama said the Bank’s latest monetary policy and operational reforms would strengthen its capacity to manage any liquidity pressures arising from such payments. “There was a sinking fund that was put up. We were very much aware of that. As a matter of fact, with the decision we are taking today, we are in a better position to manage the liquidity impact of some of those that can arise in the future,” he said. He added that the central bank was closely monitoring developments to ensure that the repayments did not undermine its monetary policy objectives. “So we have our eyes on the ball here,” Dr Asiama said. The comments come as the government continues to honour obligations to domestic bondholders under its debt management programme, including early repayment arrangements that could inject liquidity into the financial system. The Bank of Ghana has meanwhile reduced the Monetary Policy Rate by 300 basis points to 11 per cent and introduced reforms to its monetary operations framework, including narrowing the policy corridor to plus or minus 100 basis points around the policy rate. The reforms are expected to strengthen liquidity management and improve the transmission of monetary policy signals to money market rates. The central bank says it will continue monitoring liquidity conditions and developments in the financial market to ensure stability as the economy transitions to a lower interest rate environment.
