items.title: MPC reduces policy rate to 11% from 14 percent
items.description: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Bank of Ghana (BoG) has cut its Monetary Policy Rate by 300 basis points to 11 per cent, as improving economic conditions and declining market interest rates provide room for further easing of monetary policy. The reduction from 14 per cent was announced by Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Asiama, following the 133rd Monetary Policy Committee meeting held from November 16 to 18, 2026. The decision comes amid sustained improvements in domestic economic activity, easing credit conditions and expectations that inflation will gradually return to the central bank’s medium-term target. Dr Asiama said the committee had observed significant improvements in the economy, with growth remaining firm and supported by an expansion in private sector credit. “Taken together, the Committee noted significant improvements in domestic macroeconomic conditions. Domestic growth has remained firm, supported by easing credit conditions and expansion of private sector credit, and is expected to continue for the remainder of the year,” he said. The Governor explained that prevailing market interest rates had fallen below the existing policy rate of 14 per cent, indicating that the effective monetary policy stance was already lower than the announced rate. He said recent reforms to the Bank’s monetary operations framework had strengthened liquidity management and improved the transmission of monetary policy signals to money market rates. “Recent reforms to the Bank’s monetary operations framework have strengthened liquidity management and improved the transmission of monetary policy signals to money market rates,” Dr Asiama said. The committee has consequently introduced additional reforms to the monetary operations framework, including replacing the current open market operations instrument with a seven-day instrument and narrowing the monetary policy corridor from plus or minus 400 basis points to plus or minus 100 basis points around the policy rate. The reduction in the policy rate is expected to further ease borrowing costs and support businesses and households as credit conditions improve. Growth in private sector credit increased to 37.2 per cent in October 2026 from 13.9 per cent a year earlier, while real private sector credit growth rose to 30 per cent from 5.4 per cent over the same period. Banks’ average lending rates also declined to 15.8 per cent in October from 22.2 per cent in October 2025. Headline inflation, however, increased marginally to 5.5 per cent in October from 5.2 per cent in September, although it remained below the lower bound of the Bank’s medium-term target. The Bank said inflation was expected to gradually move back into the target range over the medium term, but identified risks including crude oil price shocks, the impact of El Niño on food production and quarterly adjustments in utility tariffs. On the external front, gross international reserves stood at US$12.1 billion as of November 17, 2026, equivalent to 4.4 months of import cover, down from US$13.8 billion at the end of December 2025. The next Monetary Policy Committee meeting is scheduled for January 2027.

items.title: Conakry : une opération de recensement des dos-d’âne irréguliers engagée par l’ANASUR
items.description: L’Agence nationale de surveillance des routes (ANASUR) a lancé une opération de recensement des ralentisseurs installés sans autorisation préalable sur les routes de Conakry. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans une démarche de contrôle des aménagements routiers non conformes et de réduction des dangers auxquels ils exposent les usagers. Dans le cadre de cette mission, les agents déployés sur le terrain effectuent des relevés techniques portant notamment sur l’identification, les dimensions et la localisation géographique des dos-d’âne concernés. L’opération est conduite sous la tutelle du ministère des Infrastructures. À travers ce travail de terrain, l’agence entend mettre en lumière les risques liés à la construction anarchique des ralentisseurs. En effet, des ouvrages réalisés sans tenir compte des normes techniques, notamment en matière de dimensions et de signalisation, peuvent entraîner une détérioration des chaussées et favoriser la survenue d’accidents de la circulation. L’ANASUR précise que toute installation de ralentisseur sur une voie publique doit impérativement faire l’objet d’une autorisation délivrée par les autorités compétentes. Les personnes qui enfreignent cette disposition sont passibles des sanctions prévues par la loi L/2016/074/AN portant protection du patrimoine routier national. En outre, l’agence appelle les conducteurs d’automobiles et de motocyclettes à faire preuve de responsabilité en respectant les prescriptions du Code de la route et les limitations de vitesse. Elle exhorte également les populations riveraines à porter à la connaissance des services compétents les endroits où les excès de vitesse constituent une menace pour la sécurité des usagers. Ces signalements permettront d’évaluer les besoins et d’envisager des aménagements adaptés. items.title: Senate urges FG to implement report on death of 37 miners in NSCDC custody
items.description: The Senate has urged the Federal Government to expedite action on the implementation of the recommendations of its investigative committee on the death of 37 young artisanal miners in the custody of Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Niger Command. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the resolution followed the consideration of a motion sponsored by Sen. Sani Musa (APC-Niger East) over the death of the miners on Sept. 17 in Minna, Niger. The senate called for appropriate sanctions against the officers found culpable and institutional reforms within NSCDC to prevent a recurrence of the incident. It also resolved to constitute a delegation to pay a condolence visit to the bereaved families. The lawmakers further directed the Committees on Interior, Solid Minerals, Human Rights, Police Affairs and Judiciary to monitor implementation of the investigative committee’s recommendations and report progress to the senate. Presenting the motion, Musa said the deceased were arrested during operations against suspected illegal mining activities but subsequently died under circumstances that raised concerns about their conditions of detention and protection of fundamental human rights. He said that the federal government had established a 10-member independent investigative committee, chaired by Mr Jonathan Kure, to establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths, determine responsibility and recommend appropriate measures. Musa noted that the committee had submitted its report, identifying lapses and recommending sanctions, institutional reforms and financial compensation for the families of the deceased. Seconding the motion, Sen. Ned Nwoko (APC-Delta North) described the incident as a national tragedy but called for an objective examination of the circumstances surrounding the deaths. “It is a national tragedy when so many young lives are lost under circumstances such as the ones we are discussing,” Nwoko said. He, however, observed that similar incidents involving young people allegedly engaged in illegal activities occurred in oil-producing communities in the South-South. “I believe we should apply the same standards when dealing with issues of this nature. A human life is a human life, irrespective of where the incident occurs,” he said. Responding, the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, said the motion was necessary to bring the incident to national attention and commended the federal government for establishing an investigative panel. Akpabio said the senate should not prejudge the outcome of the investigation but must recognise the circumstances surrounding the deaths. “Under Nigerian law, every person is presumed innocent until proven guilty,” he said. The senate president added that the deceased had not been given the opportunity to defend themselves before a competent court. “They are Nigerians who were not given the opportunity to defend themselves. They died under tragic and questionable circumstances, and an investigation is ongoing,” he said. NAN reports that the senate subsequently adopted the five prayers of the motion, including observing a minute silence in honour of the deceased. (NAN) The post Senate urges FG to implement report on death of 37 miners in NSCDC custody appeared first on Vanguard News .

Así, los 321.684 recién nacidos son 3.679 más que los bebés registrados en 2024, según los datos publicados este miércoles por el Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE). Esto supone una subida del 1,2%. Pese a ello, las cifras siguen siendo mucho más bajas que hace años: en concreto, son un 23,5% menos que los nacidos en 2015; y un 31% menos que en 2005. Una tendencia que los expertos atribuyen, por un lado, a que las generaciones de mujeres en edad de ser madres ahora son poco numerosas y, por lo tanto, es normal que esto se traduzca en menos nacimientos. Y, por otro, a que cada vez se tienen menos hijos, y se tienen más tarde. En este contexto, si hay un factor que explica el crecimiento demográfico en España, cerca ya de alcanzar los 50 millones de habitantes , es la inmigración. items.description: By Efe Onodjae The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has clarified that his recent meetings with members of the United States Congress in Washington, DC, were not intended to secure endorsements for his political ambition. Obi, who made the clarification in a statement posted on his Facebook page, said reports suggesting that his engagements with American lawmakers amounted to endorsements of his political aspirations were inaccurate. He explained that the visit was primarily aimed at engaging congressional leaders and other influential American stakeholders on issues concerning Nigeria’s development, citizens’ welfare and the consolidation of democracy. The post read; “I wish to address the inaccurate interpretation presented in certain media reports concerning my recent engagements with members of the United States Congress in Washington, DC. “As I expressly noted in my remarks, my visit to the United States was not intended to secure an endorsement, and I did not characterise my meetings as endorsements of my political aspirations by the US Congress or any of its members. “The primary purpose of the visit was to engage with congressional leaders and other influential American stakeholders, exchange perspectives, and discuss matters related to Nigeria’s development, the welfare of our citizens and, most importantly, the consolidation of our democracy. “I am especially concerned with strengthening democratic institutions, advancing accountability, and ensuring that Nigeria’s electoral process produces elections that are free, fair, transparent and credible. These matters should concern every Nigerian who is committed to our country’s future. “I consider engagements of this kind valuable, and I encourage other Nigerian political leaders, especially those seeking public office, to pursue similar discussions with international stakeholders. Our democracy can be strengthened through constructive dialogue, the exchange of experiences and a shared commitment to credible elections.“ The post 2027: My US congressional meetings not for endorsement — Obi appeared first on Vanguard News .

Gouvernance locale: Le Bureau du Citoyen officiellement installé à Agbodrafo
items.description: Aného, 18 nov. (ATOP) – Le Bureau du citoyen (BDC), instance indépendante d’écoute, de médiation et d’orientation, a été officiellement installé, le mardi 17 novembre à Agbodrafo, au palais royal du chef canton . Le mandat des membres est fixé à trois ans, renouvelable trois fois. Une durée qui inscrit cette mission dans la continuité et permet d’envisager un accompagnement durable des préoccupations citoyennes. La cérémonie s’est déroulée au palais royal du chef canton d’Agbodrafo, en présence des chefs de villages et des membres des Comités villageois de développement (CVD) de l’ensemble du ressort territorial. Ce cadre permanent vise à promouvoir la transparence dans la gestion des affaires publiques et à encourager l’implication active des populations dans le développement socio-économique de la commune. Sur le plan organisationnel, le Bureau du Citoyen dispose d’un siège et est placé sous l’autorité hiérarchique du maire. Il est dirigé par un coordonnateur, Agbekoué Koffi, assisté d’une rapporteuse, Mme Bocna Rebécala. L’équipe ainsi mise en place aura la responsabilité d’assurer le fonctionnement de cette structure et de faciliter les échanges entre les citoyens et les instances communales. Avec l’installation de ce Bureau du Citoyen, la commune Lacs 3 se dote ainsi d’un nouvel instrument de dialogue et de participation à la gouvernance locale. Le défi sera désormais de faire vivre cette structure au quotidien, en garantissant son accessibilité, son écoute et sa capacité à assurer le relais des préoccupations des populations auprès des autorités compétentes. Le Bureau du Citoyen est un organe indépendant mis en place pour faciliter le dialogue entre les autorités communales et les populations. Il constitue un espace où chaque citoyen peut exprimer ses préoccupations, formuler des propositions, solliciter des orientations ou faire part de ses difficultés en rapport avec la gestion des affaires locales. ATOP/AAK/SED

items.title: How FG selects Nigerians for Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Programme (NFSP) ₦100,000 grant, Social intervention.
items.description: The World Bank through its Hope for Indigenous Family Support Initiative is supporting the Federal Government to implement the Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Programme (NFSP) using the Social Safety Net System to identify poor and vulnerable Nigerian households for social intervention programmes, including the ₦100,000 Nigeria Family Support Programme NFSP. The Programme , coordinated by the Hope for Indigenous Family Support Initiative’s Coordinating Office as mandated by the Federal Ministry of Youth Development is a Nigeria grassroots empowerment, and social intervention initiative programme under President Tinubu addressing economic hardship, rising food prices and the impacts of necessary economic reforms and subsidy removals. The Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Programme (NFSP) is a cash transfer programme. It aims to mitigate the adverse effects of economic reform measures for the most vulnerable families in Nigeria. The Initiative’s role came into focus following the Federal Government’s announcement through the Federal Ministry of Youth Development of the NFSP programme on September 10, 2026, under which selected beneficiaries are to receive ₦100,000 in family financial support. Announcing the intervention, the Federal Ministry of Youth Development, said it was designed to ease the burden of rising living costs on vulnerable households.0:12 / 1:0 How FG identifies beneficiaries The integration of NIN records is expected to strengthen identity verification, reduce duplication and improve the accuracy of household information used for the social intervention programme. How Will New Beneficiaries Be Selected? The Federal Ministry through the Hope for Indigenous Family Support Initiative has clarified that selection is based on verified identity records and other relevant family and employment information for the NFSP cash transfer. the selection process involves: 1.Identifying eligible households through the Social Safety Net Systems. 2.Using verified national identity records. 3.Assessing households based on poverty and vulnerability criteria. 4.Selecting beneficiaries in phases across the six geopolitical zones. The programme covers a finite number of households in each phase. This means beneficiaries will not all receive payments at the same time. If you have not received a notification, it does not necessarily mean you have been permanently excluded from the programme. How Will the ₦100,000 Cash Transfer Be Paid? Payments are processed and payed to beneficiaries submitted bank accounts : Selected beneficiaries will receive an SMS notification from their designated payment provider. The phone number used for the notification will be obtained from the records used during the beneficiary selection process. Recipients are expected to follow the instructions in the message and provide the required consent before the money is credited to their submitted bank accounts. Who Is Eligible for the NFSP ₦100,000 Cash Transfer? Must be a Nigerian citizen by birth. Must have National Identification number NIN as a valid form of identification to be validated with NIMC. Must be at least 18-65 years old at the time of registration. The programme targets poor and vulnerable households identified through the Social Safety Nets Systems and verified national identity records. Selection is based on the government’s poverty and vulnerability criteria. How to Register and become a Beneficiary The official registration portal is nfsp.ng/signup where individuals can submit their details to become beneficiaries. Important Information for Nigerians The Federal Ministry of Youth and Development has advised Nigerians to be careful of individuals and bloggers defaming and attacking the credibility of the program and also claiming they can secure access to the cash transfer. Take note of the following: The Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Program NFSP is a social intervention and development programme . Do not pay anyone to add your name to the beneficiary list. Only selected beneficiaries will receive official SMS notifications from the approved payment providers. 3. Do not pay an individual or agent to release your ₦100,000 grant. 4. Not receiving a message immediately does not mean you have been permanently excluded. 5. The programme involves a structured process designed to identify households facing poverty and vulnerability. For inquiries or further clarification, beneficiaries should contact the official NFSP official email help@nfsp.ng or through the Federal ministry’s recognized communication channels. Nigerians do not need to register through an unofficial website or pay anyone to qualify for this intervention. Beneficiaries are selected through the official NFSP registration portal’s social safety systems and verification process. SIGNED: MANAGEMENT BOARD The post How FG selects Nigerians for Nigeria Family Strengthening and Development Programme (NFSP) ₦100,000 grant, Social intervention. appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Xiaomi Carnival Promises Up to ₦10 Million in Prizes, Plus a Chance to Win 100% Cashback
items.description: The end of the year is a time to celebrate what we have achieved, reconnect with the people who matter, and look ahead to what comes next. It is also a time when a long-planned purchase can finally feel possible. This festive season, Xiaomi Nigeria is making that moment even more rewarding with Xiaomi Carnival , a campaign that brings the excitement of Black Friday and Christmas together. Running from November 16 to December 25, 2026 , Xiaomi Carnival offers shoppers more ways to save across selected devices, alongside gifts and opportunities to win. Whether they are buying their first smartphone, replacing one that has served them for years, or choosing a thoughtful gift, shoppers can find an option that suits both their needs and their budget. The offers make everyday value part of the celebration. Shoppers can enjoy ₦10,000 off REDMI A7Pro, get the Redmi 15C with a cooking oil. A Redmi A7 is accompanied by a complimentary detergent pack; the Redmi 17 purchase comes with a gift box, while selected Redmi Note 17 Series purchases include Redmi Buds 6 Play… and the rewards do not end at checkout. After buying an eligible Xiaomi product and completing a raffle entry, shoppers have the chance to win through six Friday draws . Each week, ₦1.5 million worth of cashback and prizes will be up for grabs, including opportunities to win 100% cashback . The campaign will culminate in a grand finale, where one lucky winner will take home Xiaomi products worth ₦2.5 million . For some shoppers, the right new phone means making more room for the photos they want to keep. For others, it means a smoother way to work, study, stay connected, or share the season with family and friends. Xiaomi Carnival brings together practical savings and the possibility of an extra surprise, making a purchase they have been considering feel even more worthwhile. To participate, customers will need to scan the campaign QR code and complete the registration process by providing: Their device’s IMEI number. The name of the authorised store where the product was purchased. Their phone number. A smiling selfie. The registration process helps verify qualifying purchases made through authorised Xiaomi retail partners and ensures customers are entered into the grand prize selection. At the end of the campaign, Xiaomi Nigeria will select one lucky winner to take home Xiaomi products worth ₦2.5 million . With weekly rewards, the possibility of 100% cashback, and a grand prize to look forward to, Xiaomi Carnival gives customers more than one reason to participate. Xiaomi Carnival’s smartphone offers start with the REDMI A7 3GB+64GB at ₦153,900 . The REDMI A7 Pro is available at ₦169,900 for the 4GB+64GB version and ₦179,900 for the 4GB+128GB version. items.title: US strategist removes posts on Tinubu, Trump security partnership
items.description: American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has deleted a series of posts detailing her engagement with the Nigerian government and the security cooperation between Nigeria and the United States. The posts, which were no longer available on her X account as of Wednesday morning, included photographs of her at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, where she was seen with President Bola Tinubu and his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila. In another post, London described the security partnership between Nigeria and the US as one that was “delivering results”, crediting the relationship between Tinubu and US President Donald Trump. “The U.S.-Nigeria security partnership is delivering results. Peace through strength. None of this happens without the ongoing partnership between President Trump and President Tinubu, their steadfast commitment to eliminating terrorists, and Nigeria’s willingness to work closely with the U.S. government,” she wrote. “Because of the success of their partnership and relationship, the economic and trade opportunities are endless. The best is yet to come. Nigeria is the United States’ greatest ally in Africa,” London stated. In a separate post, she expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with people representing Nigeria, particularly on efforts to protect religious groups and strengthen relations between the two governments. “It has been an honour to work on the team of people representing Nigeria and helping to protect religious groups and further the relationship between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government,” she wrote. The reason for their deletion was not immediately known, as London had not publicly explained the move as of the time of filing this report. items.title: AVE : Les élèves d’Assahoun sensibilisés à la culture de la tolérance
items.description: Kévé, 18 nov. (ATOP) – Les élèves du lycée d’Assahoun ont été sensibilisés à la tolérance, le mardi 17 novembre dans la localité, à l’occasion de la célébration de la journée internationale de la tolérance. Placée sous le thème « Faisons des réseaux sociaux, un espace de tolérance », cette activité est initiée par le ministère en charge des Droits humains, à travers la direction de la Formation civique. Elle vise à susciter une prise de conscience collective sur la nécessité de promouvoir le respect et le vivre-ensemble, notamment dans les espaces numériques. Il s’agit de promouvoir l’acceptation des différences à travers les actes, les comportements et les paroles, afin de contribuer à la construction d’une société plus juste et pacifique. Les échanges ont porté sur les comportements répréhensibles sur Internet, notamment la diffusion de fausses informations, les atteintes à la vie privée, le cyberharcèlement, les propos haineux et la piraterie informatique. Le formateur, Daniel Agano, s’est servi des images d’illustration des actes d’intolérance sur des bâches pour toucher toutes les formes d’intolérance en cours dans les sociétés. Il a rappelé que la journée internationale pour la tolérance a été instituée par une déclaration de principes des États membres de l’UNESCO depuis le 16 novembre 1995. Elle vise, poursuit le formateur, à contribuer à l’instauration du respect et de l’appréciation de la richesse et de la diversité des cultures du monde. « Les nombreux conflits qui déchirent le monde trouvent leur origine dans l’intolérance religieuse, le genre, les idées, le rang social, l’opinion politique. Il fallait trouver un moyen pour arrêter cette attitude qui compromettait le vivre-ensemble », a expliqué M. Agano. Le représentant de la direction de la Formation civique, M. Tchakpala Olivier, a déclaré que « cette journée est une occasion de promouvoir la tolérance, une condition sine qua non au vivre ensemble ». Il a fait savoir que les actes d’intolérance sont aujourd’hui transposés sur les réseaux sociaux, et c’est l’occasion d’attirer l’attention des jeunes sur les actes inciviques qui se développent sur ces réseaux. Le proviseur du lycée d’Assahoun, Vignon Kokou, a invité les élèves à une bonne utilisation des réseaux sociaux pour préserver la cohésion sociale. ATOP/HKM/MD/BV

items.title: Bas-mono : le préfet à la rencontre des forces vives de sa juridiction
items.description: Afagnagan, 18 nov. (ATOP) – Le préfet de Bas-Mono, Colonel Akagna Kodjo a achevé le mardi 17 novembre à Kpétsou, dans la commune Bas-Mono1, sa tournée de prise de contact et d’information avec les populations des différents cantons de sa juridiction. Démarrée le 11 novembre dernier, cette démarche s’inscrit dans la dynamique de renforcement des liens de collaboration entre l’administration préfectorale et les communautés à la base. Ce périple a conduit le préfet et sa délégation à Afagnan-Gbléta, Afagnagan, Attitogon, Hompou, Agbétiko, Agome-Glozou, et puis Kpétsou. Il lui a permis de se faire connaitre des populations, de s’imprégner des réalités du terrain et d’écouter les préoccupations de ses administrés. Le préfet a saisi l’occasion pour partager sa vision pour le développement du milieu avec les populations. Dans chaque localité visitée, le préfet a échangé avec les chefs traditionnels, les leaders communautaires, les responsables des comités de développement à la base (CDQ, CVD et CCD). Il a entretenu ses auditoires sur le développement local, l’unité et le respect mutuel. Il a insisté sur la sécurité des personnes et des biens, la lutte contre l’extrémisme violent en invitant les populations à signaler toute personne étrangère aux autorités compétentes. Le représentant du pouvoir central a rassuré ses administrés de sa disponibilité à travailler avec tous les acteurs pour le développement de la préfecture tout en conviant ses interlocuteurs à la participation aux travaux communautaires, à plus de collaboration avec l’administration. Les chefs des cantons et les populations ont salué la démarche du préfet et évoqué plusieurs préoccupations, notamment l’état des pistes rurales, l’accès à l’eau potable, à la santé, l’éducation, ainsi que l’accompagnement des activités agricoles. Elles se sont engagées à l’accompagner pour la réussite de sa mission. ATOP/DK/AR/BV

items.title: Oti/Artisanat : La CPM adopte son budget prévisionnel de 2027
items.description: Mango, 18 nov. (ATOP) – La Chambre préfectorale des métiers (CPM) de l’Oti a tenu son assemblée générale ordinaire, le lundi 16 novembre à Mango, dans la commune Oti 1. Les travaux ont porté notamment sur la présentation du budget prévisionnel 2027 et des activités programmées pour le prochain exercice. La rencontre est initiée par le nouveau bureau exécutif élu en août dernier. Elle vise à rendre compte aux délégués des huit cantons de la préfecture des activités réalisées et à venir, ainsi qu’à échanger sur les difficultés du secteur artisanal et les pistes de solutions. Le budget prévisionnel présenté fait état de recettes estimées à 5.930.000 F CFA, provenant notamment de la vente de fiches de contrat, de l’établissement des cartes professionnelles et d’apprentissage, ainsi que de la subvention de l’État. Les dépenses sont évaluées à 4.255.000 F CFA et concernent, entre autres, l’acquisition de matériel informatique et de fournitures de bureau, les charges salariales, les formations, les missions et les œuvres sociales. Au titre des activités de 2027 figurent des sensibilisations sur le rôle des chambres de métiers et l’importance de la carte professionnelle, des formations sur l’hygiène, la qualité et la sécurité au travail, des opérations de reboisement, le recensement des entrepreneurs, la réhabilitation du bar-restaurant du centre des artisans, ainsi que des expositions et foires de produits locaux. Des actions en faveur de l’inclusion des personnes en situation de handicap et des rencontres avec les partenaires sont également prévues. Les délégués ont formulé des doléances, notamment la réduction des frais d’établissement des cartes professionnelles et d’apprentissage. L’adjoint au maire de Oti 1, Dantoukou Bouraima, a salué la tenue de cette assemblée, soulignant le rôle du secteur artisanal dans l’économie nationale. Il a réaffirmé la disponibilité de la commune à accompagner la CPM dans ses activités. Le président régional de la Chambre des métiers des Savanes, Damesonon Sambiani, a exhorté les artisans à œuvrer pour la modernisation des ateliers, la qualification des apprentis et un meilleur accès aux financements et aux marchés publics. Le président de la CPM-Oti, Lanzaré Soulemane, a appelé les artisans à la solidarité et à la discipline pour dynamiser un secteur créateur de richesses et d’emplois. Il a rassuré les délégués que leurs doléances seront transmises aux autorités compétentes et réaffirmé l’engagement de son bureau à promouvoir l’artisanat dans la préfecture. ATOP/TT/JK/SED

items.title: Africa Education Watch urges Education Ministry to intervene in Rent Control-UGEL dispute
items.description: Executive Director of Africa Education Watch, Kofi Asare, has called on the Ministry of Education to urgently intervene in the disagreement between the Rent Control Department and the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL) over hostel rents. His comments follow an incident in which the Acting Rent Commissioner, Frederick Opoku, nearly got into a physical altercation with a hostel manager at the University of Ghana during the inspection at UGEL. The confrontation reportedly followed a disagreement after Mr Opoku inspected the hostel facilities. Speaking on Joy FM’s Midday News on Wednesday, November 18, he said the Ministry should have been involved from the beginning, alongside Rent Control, the Parliamentary Select Committee on Education and university authorities. This, he explained, is because the Select Committee approves rates, including the rent. He added that the stakeholders needed to examine UGEL’s cost structure and profit margins to determine whether hostel rents could reasonably be reduced. I think the Ministry of Education has a key role to play here. At the point of entry, Rent Control should have been working closely with the Ministry of Education, the Parliamentary Select Committee on Education, and the university authorities. And so all three bodies should have sat down and then went through the standardised build-up…Without that constructive engagement, it is impossible to make any progress in terms of reduction in rent,” he said. Mr Asare said his organisation had advised about two months ago that the relevant stakeholders should engage to resolve the matter, but that had not happened. He also criticised the approach adopted during recent Rent Control inspections, arguing that confrontations, verbal exchanges and public demonstrations would not address the underlying concerns. “Waving around with cameras and bloggers and all that is not the solution to the problem we want to solve,” he said. He added that hostel porters and managers were not responsible for determining rental rates, insisting that discussions should instead involve the institutions with the authority to influence the charges. Mr Asare therefore urged the stakeholders to move beyond public exchanges and begin direct engagement on the cost of accommodation and possible rent reductions.

items.title: Université Joseph-Ki-Zerbo: Le camarade Souleymane Simporé obtient le grade de docteur
items.description: Le camarade Souleymane Simporé a soutenu sa thèse de doctorat unique en Lettres modernes, le jeudi 12 novembre 2026, dans la salle de réunion des écoles doctorales de l’université Joseph-Ki-Zerbo sur le thème : « Approche éco-étho-sémiotique des innovations environnementales au Burkina Faso : entre éco-formation, non formelle et changement de comportements ». Après avoir jugé le travail recevable, le jury lui a attribué la mention très honorable à l’issue de la soutenance. La mention très honorable a été attribuée au ‘’désormais’’ docteur Souleymane Simporé à l’issue de la soutenance de sa thèse de doctorat unique en Lettres modernes, le jeudi 12 novembre 2026, à l’université Joseph-Ki-Zerbo sur le thème : « Approche éco-étho-sémiotique des innovations environnementales au Burkina Faso : entre éco-formation, non formelle et changement de comportements ». Selon le président du jury, Josph Paré, professeur titulaire à l’université Joseph-Ki-Zerbo, le travail soumis par le camarade Souleymane Simporé dans le cadre de l’obtention du grade de docteur à l’attention du jury a été bien apprécié par l’ensemble du Jury. « La thèse fournit de nombreuses informations qui mettent en relief des enjeux théoriques très importants en matière de formation, d’éco-formation et de transformation des comportements. Le choix orienté vers la sémiotique permet sans aucun doute de voir comment cet outil d’analyse des signes et des comportements au sein d’une société permet de mesurer l’ampleur des changements et la manière dont les innovations peuvent s’insérer dans une société, au sein d’un groupe donné. L’approche prend en considération l’ensemble des zones de production de notre pays. On se rend compte qu’en dépit de la différenciation des zones, les communautés s’approprient un certain nombre d’innovations et de transformations en vue de permettre à ces sociétés d’avancer. C’est un travail de portée scientifique », a-t-il précisé. Le professeur des écoles, Souleymane Simporé (milieu), obtient le grade de docteur avec la mention très honorable. Le directeur de thèse, le maître de conférences Kpanyawne Somda Thadée Balouhib a surtout apprécié la méthode de travail de l’impétrant. Il est parti de la littérature pour aboutir sur un terrain scientifique. Selon lui, les littéraires ne sont pas que des littéraires, ils construisent surtout des humains, ils fabriquent des outils, mais des outils humains. « Le camarade Souleymane Simporé a développé les comportements et les comportements relèvent des sciences humaines qui sont en elles-mêmes la conscience des autres sciences. Si les humains avaient intégré les formations des littéraires, on n’allait pas voir aujourd’hui, un frère prendre une arme contre un autre frère. La formation humaine est une tâche dévolue aux Hommes des sciences humaines. N’oublions pas que Science sans conscience n’est que ruine de l’âme », a-t-il ajouté. Tout heureux, docteur Souleymane Simporé a précisé que son étude propose une approche éco-étho-sémiotique comme cadre d’analyse des innovations environnementales au Burkina Faso, notamment en milieu paysan. Selon lui, le défi est d’articuler la science du développement avec les savoirs endogènes et l’imaginaire burkinabè pour promouvoir l’écocitoyenneté ». Il faut préciser que le travail de recherche de l’impétrant a abouti à des résultats exploitables dans le domaine de la construction de notre société . « Dans nos établissements scolaires par exemple, le jardin scolaire est un cadre d’éco-formation. Contrairement à ce qu’on croit, le jardin scolaire ne doit pas se limiter à la fourniture de condiments à la cantine scolaire. Non, son importance va au-delà. Il est un cadre d’éco-formation qui peut amener les paysans à contribuer d’une manière durable à concrétiser les formations formelles reçues dans les salles de classe », a affirmé docteur Souleymane Simporé. L’impétrant est présentement en exercice dans la région des Koulsé en tant que professeur des écoles. Adama de Maliki malikadams020@gmail.com

items.title: Cinkassé/Artisanat : La CPM fait le bilan de ses activités et planifie des actions futures
items.description: Cinkassé, 17 nov. (ATOP) – Les membres et sympathisants de la Chambre préfectorale des métiers (CPM) de Cinkassé ont tenu, le mardi 17 novembre à Cinkassé, leur assemblée générale ordinaire, consacrée au bilan des activités et à la planification des actions futures de leur institution. Cette rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre du pilotage des activités de la chambre et se tient conformément aux textes régissant les chambres de métiers. Elle a permis aux participants d’échanger sur les stratégies visant à améliorer le secteur de l’artisanat dans la préfecture. Les acteurs ont validé le Plan d’action opérationnel (PAO) 2027 de la chambre et adopté son budget prévisionnel. Ce plan prévoit notamment des actions en faveur de la modernisation des ateliers, du renforcement des compétences et de la valorisation du savoir-faire des artisans. D’un montant de 12.521.200 F CFA, le budget prévisionnel sera consacré à la mise en œuvre d’activités concrètes susceptibles de produire des impacts positifs sur le terrain. Le préfet de Cinkassé, colonel Yanani Tiékabe, a souligné l’importance du secteur de l’artisanat dans l’économie nationale. Il a invité les artisans à faire preuve de professionnalisme et à promouvoir l’innovation dans leurs productions. Le secrétaire général de la Chambre régionale des métiers des Savanes, Kassou Adjéoda, et le président de la CPM de Cinkassé, Kariyiaré Nibembane, ont exhorté les participants à privilégier des débats constructifs, afin de faire de la chambre un modèle de réussite et d’innovation. La rencontre s’est déroulée en présence de plusieurs autorités politiques et administratives, dont l’inspecteur du travail et des lois sociales de Cinkassé, Nandjak Kpingmame. ATOP/BB/JK/AR

items.title: Irak : bras de fer explosif entre Bagdad et les Kataeb Hezbollah sur le contrôle des armes
items.description: Le gouvernement irakien et les Kataeb Hezbollah, puissante milice chiite proche de l'Iran, se defient ouvertement. Le 16 novembre, le Premier ministre irakien Ali al-Zaïdi a ordonne a l'armee de se preparer a entrer dans Jurf al-Sakhr, a une cinquantaine de kilometres au sud de Bagdad. Ce bastion controle depuis plus de dix ans par le groupe arme pourrait devenir le theâtre d'une confrontation entre forces irakiennes. Bagdad exige le retrait des miliciens d'ici la fin de la semaine. Mais le 17 novembre, l'un de leurs responsables, Abou Taleb al-Saïdi, a prevenu qu'ils ne quitteraient pas les lieux, meme sous la contrainte. Les troupes gouvernementales ont renforce leur presence aux abords du district, sans y lancer d'assaut a ce stade. L'Iran en mediateur Le differend s'est aggrave apres une enquete officielle sur un trafic presume de petrole dans cette zone. Les autorites accusent des reseaux lies a la milice de detourner des ressources publiques ; neuf responsables de la securite et du secteur petrolier ont ete limoges. Kataeb Hezbollah rejette les accusations et denonce un pretexte destine a la contraindre au desarmement. Depuis son arrivee au pouvoir, Ali al-Zaïdi veut retablir le monopole de l'etat sur les armes, avec une echeance fixee au 30 juin 2027. L'objectif se heurte aux factions pro-iraniennes, dont certaines disposent de leurs propres combattants, arsenaux et relais politiques. Washington soutient la demarche de Bagdad, apres les attaques de milices contre des interets americains et des pays du Golfe. Face au risque d'affrontements entre groupes chiites, les mediations s'intensifient. Esmaïl Qaani, commandant de la force Al-Qods des Gardiens de la revolution iraniens, s'est rendu a Bagdad le 16 novembre. Des sources evoquent une possible issue negociee, mais aucun retrait effectif n'est confirme. Au-dela de Jurf al-Sakhr, c'est la capacite de l'etat irakien a exercer son autorite face aux groupes armes qui est en jeu.

items.title: Attal, Retailleau et Lisnard esquissent une primaire sans Philippe
items.description: Les representants des trois candidats ont avance le 17 novembre sur l'organisation d'une primaire destinee a designer un champion commun face au risque d'elimination des le premier tour. L'ancien Premier ministre edouard Philippe, lui, s'y oppose toujours fermement. Des dates en janvier et un vote a deux euros Reunis en fin d'apres-midi, les directeurs de campagne de Renaissance, des Republicains et de Nouvelle energie ont converge sur plusieurs points. La primaire, « la plus ouverte possible », se deroulerait a deux tours, soit les 17 et 24 janvier, soit les 24 et 31 janvier. Un tel scrutin preliminaire a la presidentielle avait deja ete propose par Bruno Retailleau, il y a une semaine . Le vote serait essentiellement electronique, avec une participation de deux euros et quelques bureaux physiques par departement. Des parrainages d'elus et une charte de valeurs centre-droit restent a preciser, tout comme le format des debats televises. Une nouvelle reunion est prevue la semaine prochaine. Chez LR, on assure que « personne n'a pose la participation d'edouard Philippe comme un prealable » et que « la primaire pourrait tres bien avoir lieu » sans lui. L'entourage d'Attal (Renaissance) espere encore un revirement, tandis que David Lisnard, invite le 18 novembre sur TF1, a durci le ton : la presence du maire du Havre est « indispensable » et il faut « lui mettre la pression ». ▶️ Primaire de la droite et du centre : 🗣️ "Il faut que la compétition de la primaire, qui n'est pas un accord de gouvernement mais une sélection, soit la plus large possible. Y compris avec Gabriel Attal et, s'ils respectent les conditions de la primaire, Nicolas Dupont-Aignan et Reconquête. Édouard Philippe est indispensable, on doit lui mettre la pression" @davidlisnard candidat "Nouvelle Énergie" à l’élection présidentielle — TF1Info (@TF1Info) November 18, 2026 « Dire qu'on accepterait de faire la competition sans lui, c'est lui permettre de rester tranquille sur son Aventin », a-t-il declare, tout en plaidant pour un perimetre large pouvant inclure jusqu'a eric Zemmour ou Nicolas Dupont-Aignan, sous conditions. L'equipe d'Horizons a reaffirme son opposition. Sur X, Jordan Bardella, president du Rassemblement national et soutien de Marine Le Pen, favorite du premier tour a raille ces « accords de boutique » entre « le macroniste assume (Gabriel Attal), le macroniste rallie (Bruno Retailleau) et le macroniste masque (David Lisnard) ». Primaire de la droite et du centre: "Ces accords de boutique sont très loin de la rupture attendue par les Français", selon Jordan Bardella https://t.co/6727eGydcH — BFM (@BFMTV) November 17, 2026 Alexandra Martin, secretaire generale de Nouvelle energie, a pour sa part rappele que les conditions posees « devront etre prises en compte et edouard Philippe devra en etre ». Si les contours se precisent, des divergences subsistent sur le perimetre et le caractere indispensable ou non de Philippe. Les trois camps avancent toutefois sans attendre un eventuel ralliement.

items.title: Le FLNC-UC tente de relancer la violence armée en Corse
items.description: L'attaque contre les locaux de l'Agence regionale de sante (ARS) a Bastia, qui a cause des degâts limites sans faire de blesse, est presentee comme la premiere action attribuee au Front de liberation nationale corse – Union des combattants (FLNC-UC) depuis sa conference de presse clandestine d'août. Une organisation en quete de regain d'influence Vers 1h du matin, une detonation a retenti dans le quartier du Fango a Bastia. L'engin a endommage la grille et l'entree de la Maison des affaires sociales, qui abrite l'ARS ainsi que d'autres services de l'etat. Les inscriptions « ARS Fora » (ARS dehors) et « FLNC UC » ont immediatement oriente les investigations. Le procureur de Bastia a ouvert une enquete pour destruction par moyen dangereux, rapidement reprise par le Parquet national antiterroriste, qui retient l'association de malfaiteurs en vue d'un acte de terrorisme. La ministre de la Sante Stephanie Rist s'est exprimee sur le reseau social X : « Intimider les agents du service public, c'est s'attaquer a la Republique. Nous ne laisserons jamais la violence faire la loi ». À celles et ceux qui font vivre le service public de santé en Corse, je veux dire mon soutien et ma solidarité après l’attaque qui a visé l’ARS à Bastia. Je me suis entretenue avec sa directrice générale pour lui témoigner mon soutien et celui du Gouvernement, ainsi qu’à l’ensemble de ses équipes. Aucune revendication, aucun désaccord ne peut justifier que l’on s’en prenne à ceux qui travaillent chaque jour pour la santé de nos concitoyens. Intimider les agents du service public, c’est s’attaquer à la République. Nous ne laisserons jamais la violence faire la loi. — Stéphanie RIST (@stephanie_rist) November 17, 2026 Le FLNC-UC, branche clandestine independantiste, avait tenu en août une conference de presse tres mediatisee. Une quinzaine d'hommes cagoules et armes avaient rejete le projet d'autonomie, qualifie de « mascarade », et menace les non-Corses installes sur l'île. En septembre, un communique non date du groupe avait ete rendu public . L'attaque, la premiere action concrete qui lui est attribuee depuis, intervient alors que le processus d'autonomie est bloque apres le rejet du Senat. Le groupe, heritier d'un mouvement qui a multiplie les attentats dans les annees 1970-1980 avant de connaître un declin marque par les luttes internes et le passage de certains cadres vers le banditisme, semble chercher a peser a nouveau sur le debat politique. Le depute LR de Corse Francois-Xavier Ceccoli a denonce le recours a la violence : « En democratie, on peut debattre du role autant que des politiques menees par l'ARS. Jamais user de violence pour faire passer on ne sait quel message ». Les locaux de l’ARS de Bastia ont été pris pour cible cette nuit par un attentat. Je tiens avant tout à témoigner mon soutien à sa directrice générale ainsi qu’au personnel de l’agence. En démocratie, on peut débattre du rôle autant que des politiques menées par l’ARS. Jamais user de violence pour faire passer on ne sait quel message. La Corse a besoin de sérénité autant que de politiques publiques efficaces, pas d’un retour d’une violence qui est une impasse. — François Xavier Ceccoli (@FXceccoli) November 17, 2026 Des tracts de Nazione, formation decrite comme la vitrine legale du FLNC-UC, avaient deja reclame le depart de l'ARS quelques jours plus tot. L'organisation armee, affaiblie et en manque de combattants, tente ainsi de rappeler son existence dans un contexte politique tendu, entre echec de l'autonomie et percee du Rassemblement national en Corse.

items.title: Philippine Police Detain Hundreds Protesting Trump Visit
items.description: Click to expand Image Protesters attempt to march to the ASEAN Summit venue in Manila but are stopped by hundreds of police officers, November 17, 2026. © 2026 Lian Buan/Human Rights Watch Police in the Philippines arrested and detained at least 245 people protesting the visit of US President Donald Trump to Manila for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit. Protests in Manila started on November 15 opposing the Philippine government’s plan to build a technology manufacturing hub in Capas, Tarlac province, under the US government’s “Pax Silica” initiative. The construction will displace hundreds of Indigenous people and small farmers from their homes and farmlands. An estimated 6,000 people joined the protests despite police efforts to contain demonstrations by banning them everywhere except in “freedom parks” – designated areas where rallies can be held without a permit. Yet police arrested 236 people on the outskirts of Metro Manila who were traveling from the Southern Tagalog region to the main protest site. Among those detained were 29 farmers including members of the Indigenous Mangyan tribe, 19 journalists, 9 environmental defenders, and 6 human rights workers. Ephraim Cortez of the National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers said 19 children were detained. “This is the largest mass arrest we’ve seen under [President] Marcos,” protest leader Renato Reyes told Human Rights Watch. “Our whole delegation was arrested and taken to a police camp where lawyers were not given immediate access.” Detainees are being held inside a police camp in a hall with poor ventilation, insufficient drinking water, and inadequate restroom facilities, according to activists and lawyers. The protesters have been detained for three days without charge. Lawyers representing them expressed concern that they could face criminal charges of illegal assembly, alarms and scandals, and disobedience to authority. Police detained without charge another nine protesters at the main protest site on November 15 for attempting to march to the ASEAN summit venue. News footage shows police officers slapping and kicking a protester on the ground. International human rights law protects the right to peaceful assembly. Law enforcement may not carry out indiscriminate mass arrests even if a protest violates local laws or becomes disorderly. Arrests need to be based on individualized grounds and comply with the requirements of legality, necessity, and proportionality. Police can arrest people responsible for specific unlawful conduct but not just for taking part in a protest. All those arbitrarily detained for exercising their basic rights should be immediately released.

items.title: Tinubu’s tough reforms will ensure lasting prosperity for Nigeria – Wike
items.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, has urged market traders in Abuja to rally behind President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027 for lasting prosperity. Wike, who made the call during a town hall with various market associations across the nation’s capital in Abuja on Wednesday, stressed that Tinubu administration’s economic reforms were laying the foundation for long-term national growth and stability. He acknowledged the economic difficulties triggered by the removal of the fuel subsidy but maintained that previous administrations lacked the courage to confront what he described as a systemic scam. “This country is nearly gone. For you to say that you must try to change what is happening means that you must lay a foundation first, and when you lay a foundation, you give it time to grow. “There is no government that has not identified that this oil subsidy is a scam, why university teachers cannot work, no payment of salaries, no payment of pensioners. “Everybody is afraid; they lack courage. If you don’t have good leaders who have courage to take decisions, that country will not grow,” he added. According to the minister, the temporary sacrifices necessitated by the subsidy removal have yielded tangible benefits nationwide. “This includes increased revenue allocations to states and local governments, clearance of pension backlogs, and an end to recurring strikes by the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU).” Wike cautioned Nigerians against politicians promising to reverse the subsidy removal, arguing that such rhetoric was deceptive and would set the country backwards. “If we allow these policies that the government has put in place to mature, what is going to happen in the next four years will be good. Forget about people coming to tell you stories,” he said. Highlighting his administration’s achievements in Abuja since assuming office in August 2023, Wike pointed to ongoing and completed road infrastructure projects in satellite towns and districts, noting that good road networks were critical for reducing transportation costs and boosting commerce. He pledged to grant approval for the further development of markets in the territory and promised to hold regular interactive sessions with traders at least once every six months. Beyond physical infrastructure, the minister underscored institutional reforms approved by Tinubu for the FCT, noting that for the first time since the territory’s creation in 1976, an indigene was appointed to the Federal Executive Council. He also cited the establishment of the FCT Civil Service Commission, which allows career civil servants to rise to the rank of Permanent Secretary and Head of Service, and the creation of Mandate Secretariats for Women and Youth. Dismissing ethnic and regional sentiments in governance, Wike urged the traders to judge leadership strictly by performance and tangible impact rather than tribal affiliation. “Governance has nothing to do with where I come from. It is not about Hausa, Yoruba, or Igbo; it is about, “If I do my business here, am I happy?” he stated. Wike also criticised opposition figures, faulting former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s handling of past privatisation exercises and questioning the track record of former Rivers Governor Rotimi Amaechi over uncompleted projects. Wike urged the market associations to participate in the upcoming campaign structure by nominating two representatives from each state chapter to join the campaign committee, assuring them of logistical support ahead of the 2027 general elections. Earlier, Amb. Maureen Tamuno, Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Abuja Investments Company Ltd (AICL), described the interactive forum as a landmark engagement underscoring the minister’s commitment to people-orientated governance. Tamuno commended Wike for transforming both the city centre and satellite towns through road construction and rehabilitation, noting that projects such as the Saburi Road corridor had eased commercial movement. While urging traders to take full advantage of the dialogue to air their views constructively, the AICL boss reminded them that infrastructure development came with a shared responsibility to abide by market rules and regulations. Speaking on behalf of the traders, the Chairman of the Wuse Market Traders Association, Mr Okorie Ikechukwu-Raphael, lauded the transformation of internal market roads, shop redevelopments, and the opening up of area councils across the FCT. Also, Chairman of the Arewa Traders Association, Alhaji Adamu Ibrahim, reaffirmed the readiness of northern traders to work for the electoral success of Tinubu and all allied candidates in the FCT in 2027. Highlighting the role of traders in job creation and revenue generation, Ibrahim urged the minister to grant market leaders a seat at the table when formulating market-related policies, while praising the AICL boss for proactive conflict resolution and regard for traders’ welfare. Adekambi assured the minister of the loyalty of market women, vowing that they would vote in 2027 and remain at polling units to ensure their votes counted toward the re-election of President Tinubu. items.title: Pour échapper aux régulations, Palmer Luckey veut délocaliser des activités stratégiques sur une plateforme en mer
items.description: Dans la nuit du mardi 17 au mercredi 18 novembre, Palmer Luckey, le cofondateur de l’entreprise américaine de défense Anduril, a annoncé travailler depuis plus de dix ans à la création d’une plateforme artificielle en mer baptisée « SLAB ». Selon Luckey, l’objectif est d’échapper aux lois des États et des collectivités locales qui, selon lui, entravent des industries comme la transformation des métaux, la recherche et les traitements médicaux, le dessalement, le raffinage du pétrole ou le génie chimique. SLAB n’est pas un projet isolé : le seasteading , un mouvement qui œuvre pour l’émergence de communautés autonomes en mer, en tirant profit de l’absence de souveraineté des États dans les eaux internationales, a connu une certaine popularité dans les cercles libertariens dans les années 2000 et 2010. Le mouvement est lié au Seasteading Institute, une organisation créée en 2008 par Wayne Gramlich et Patri Friedman, le petit-fils de l’économiste Milton Friedman, avec le soutien financier de Peter Thiel. L’idée a connu une résurgence au début des années 2020 sous une autre forme, celle de « l’État-réseau » ( network state ), sous l’impulsion de l’entrepreneur Balaji Srinivasan, qui a rejoint la firme de capital-risque Andreessen Horowitz en 2013 avant de devenir directeur technique de la plateforme d’échange de cryptomonnaies Coinbase en 2018, et qui figure parmi les premiers investisseurs d’Anduril. Selling Oculus to Facebook in 2014 gave me money for helicopter flight lessons and developing a seastead called SLAB with a 1,000 year design life. The goal was to be cheaper than land and absent state/local laws that cripple critical American industries like metal processing,… pic.twitter.com/aJkd0eOgLF — Palmer Luckey (@PalmerLuckey) November 18, 2026 Luckey présente SLAB comme une étape vers son « objectif de faire revivre la destinée manifeste et l’expansion vers l’Ouest ». Il ajoute : « À une époque où la plupart des adeptes du seasteading voulaient fuir les États-Unis et fumer de l’herbe, c’était le seul projet explicitement conçu pour rendre l’Amérique plus forte, une soupape de sécurité face à des règles et réglementations mal pensées ou dépassées ». Luckey dit avoir récemment réalisé, avec quelques amis, de nouveaux investissements dans SLAB, mais rejette l’idée selon laquelle la plateforme serait un simple projet de centre de données flottant pour l’intelligence artificielle. Plusieurs start-ups se sont déjà positionnées pour exploiter la mer et l’énergie générée par les vagues ou les marées au profit de centres de données, comme Panthalassa, basée à Portland, dans l’Oregon, qui a levé 140 millions de dollars en mai et bénéficie notamment du soutien de Peter Thiel. En Écosse, Mocean Energy a annoncé en juillet son projet d’installer des serveurs d’IA sur des flotteurs en mer, alimentés par les vagues, des panneaux solaires et des batteries, refroidis par l’eau de mer environnante et reliés à la terre par satellite The Long-Running Climate Reporting Saga That Is Giving Companies Whiplash », The Wall Street Journal , 16 novembre 2026.'> 1 . Afin d’échapper aux réglementations des États fédérés tout en restant dans les eaux américaines, SLAB – si le projet venait à voir le jour – devrait se trouver à au moins trois milles nautiques des côtes, soit environ 5,5 kilomètres, la limite des eaux relevant des États. Les activités de la plateforme resteraient théoriquement soumises aux normes et lois fédérales. Trump a proposé, durant la campagne pour la présidentielle de 2024, la création de « Freedom Cities », des villes nouvelles bâties sur des terres fédérales et soustraites à une partie des réglementations fédérales. Plusieurs groupes représentant des projets de villes autonomes affirment avoir rencontré des membres de l’administration Trump et échangé avec des élus dans les semaines qui ont suivi son retour au pouvoir, en janvier 2025 ‘Startup City’ Groups Say They’re Meeting Trump Officials to Push for Deregulated ‘Freedom Cities’ », Wired , 7 mars 2025.'> 2 . La Freedom Cities Coalition, créée par une société liée à Próspera, travaille notamment à la rédaction d’un projet de loi qui permettrait au Congrès d’approuver par avance la création de ces villes par des accords entre États. items.title: UGEL hostel rent dispute requires dialogue, not confrontations – Africa Education Watch
items.description: Africa Education Watch has criticised the Rent Control Department’s approach to resolving the disagreement with the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL) over hostel rental charges. Speaking on Joy FM’s Middaynews on Wednesday, November 18, the organisation’s Executive Director, Kofi Asare, said confrontations, public demonstrations and verbal exchanges with hostel managers will not address the concerns surrounding the cost of accommodation. He maintained that hostel porters and managers were not the appropriate people to engage on the matter because they do not determine rental rates. “Moving around with cameras and bloggers and all that is not the solution to the problem we want to solve,” he said. He argued that the Rent Control Department should have engaged the Ministry of Education, the Parliamentary Select Committee on Education and university authorities from the outset. According to him, the stakeholders need to examine UGEL’s cost structure and profit margins to establish whether there is room for a reduction in hostel rents. “Without that constructive engagement, it is impossible to make any progress in terms of reduction in rent,” he said. Mr Asare said Africa Education Watch had advocated such engagement about two months ago, but the recommendation was not acted upon. He is therefore urging the relevant institutions to begin direct discussions on the cost of accommodation and possible adjustments to hostel charges.

items.title: Prosecution closes case against Wontumi; court sets December 17 deadline for defence
items.description: The Accra High Court has directed former Ashanti Regional New Patriotic Party (NPP) Chairman, Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, to file a submission of no case to answer by December 17, 2026, following the closure of the prosecution’s case in the Tano Nimiri illegal mining trial. The directive gives the defence time to argue that the evidence presented by the prosecution is insufficient to require Mr Wontumi to open his defence. The case involves Mr Wontumi and Akonta Mining Company Limited over alleged illegal mining activities in the Tano Nimiri Forest Reserve. The prosecution has accused the company of undertaking mining operations in the protected forest without the required authorisation. A key witness in the trial is Edward Akuoko, a former manager of Akonta Mining Company, who was initially charged alongside Mr Wontumi but was later discharged and called as the first prosecution witness. Mr Akuoko was among five accused persons in the case until the Attorney-General’s Office withdrew all charges against him in November 2025 under Section 59 of the Criminal and Other Offences (Procedure) Act, 1960 (Act 30). His role as a prosecution witness has been a major point of contention for the defence. Mr Wontumi’s lawyers recently filed an application seeking to compel the prosecution to disclose the agreement under which Mr Akuoko was discharged and subsequently became a state witness. However, the High Court dismissed the application. Following the ruling, Mr Wontumi’s lawyer, Samuel Atta Akyea, announced plans to appeal, insisting that the agreement was a critical document that should be made available for public scrutiny. “We’ll look at it and file an appeal against the ruling because I believe this is a critical document the whole country should see to understand how the man secured his freedom,” he said. With the prosecution now having closed its case, the defence is expected to file its submission of no case to answer by December 17. A submission of no case is an application asking the court to discharge an accused person on the grounds that the prosecution has not presented sufficient evidence to establish a case requiring a defence. The court will consider the submission before deciding whether Mr Wontumi should be called upon to open his defence.

items.title: Vice President urges MTN to improve network quality and expand rural connectivity
items.description: Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has urged MTN Ghana to increase investment in network quality, customer experience and connectivity in underserved communities as the country works to widen access to digital services. She said sustained investment in telecommunications infrastructure was critical to ensuring that more Ghanaians benefit from opportunities in the country’s growing digital economy. Speaking at the MTN Ghana @30 Stakeholders Dinner in Accra, Professor Opoku-Agyemang said access to reliable and affordable connectivity should not depend on where a person lives. She disclosed that the government had allocated GH¢45 million in the 2027 Budget for rural telephony projects to extend telecommunications services to communities with limited access. “Our priority is to extend reliable and affordable connectivity to communities that remain underserved, while upgrading existing infrastructure to support digital services,” she said. The Vice President noted that improved digital infrastructure would create opportunities for businesses, education, healthcare and public service delivery. Professor Opoku-Agyemang also encouraged MTN to invest more in protecting subscribers against fraud, saying the growing use of digital financial services required stronger security measures. “MTN, I therefore encourage you to invest even more in network quality, access to underserved communities, customer service and experience, and protection against fraud,” she said. She commended the company for its 30-year contribution to Ghana’s telecommunications industry, including investments in infrastructure, employment and the digital economy. She also acknowledged the MTN Ghana Foundation’s support for initiatives in health, education and economic empowerment. The Vice President reaffirmed the government’s commitment to creating a supportive environment for private sector investment while ensuring that the benefits of technological advancement are widely shared.

items.title: Can Ghana reclaim its eco-friendly roots with the ‘takeaway’ ban?
items.description: On May 25, 2026, Ghana’s Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) issued a definitive policy directive that promises to reshape the daily routines of millions: effective January 1, 2027, the production, importation, sale, distribution, and use of expanded polystyrene foam products, universally known across West Africa as Styrofoam or ‘takeaway packs,’ will be illegal. The landmark announcement enforces a commitment originally declared by President John Dramani Mahama during the 2025 World Environment Day celebration. Covering all commercial and human activities, the ban offers exemptions only for highly specialised medical, scientific, laboratory, and diagnostic applications under strict regulatory oversight. For a nation grappling with mounting plastic waste, the measure represents an ambitious attempt to protect public health, overhaul urban sanitation, and steer Africa’s pioneer democracy toward sustainable development. The Cultural Shift: How Convenience Replaced Tradition To understand the magnitude of the impending ban, one must examine the quiet cultural transformation that swept through Ghanaian towns and cities over the past three decades. A generation ago, buying hot street food was an exercise in intuitive sustainability. Schoolchildren and workers carried lunch boxes or enamel bowls to local food vendors. Hearty portions of waakye traditionally wrapped in fresh Ketemfe leaves (Sweet Prayer Plant). The leaves not only provided an organic, biodegradable container but also infused the hot food with a subtle, aromatic flavor cherished by generations. Yet, as urban centers grew and the pace of modern life accelerated, expanded polystyrene and single-use plastic bags offered irresistible convenience. Within a few decades, these synthetic containers completely displaced traditional packaging. In doing so, they also altered social norms. The Stigma of Sustainability “Today, walking to a street food vendor with your own reusable bowl often earns you funny looks or label tags like ‘too known.’ Even newlyweds who bring home-cooked meals to work in reusable glass containers are met with lighthearted teasing. What was once common sense has been stigmatized as odd.” This subtle cultural shift created a paradox: habits that protect the environment are ridiculed, while habits that pollute the country are embraced as modern. The Liquid Commodity: From Earthenware to PET Bottles A parallel evolution occurred in drinking water packaging. Thirty years ago, drinking water was retailed in metal cups from large containers for the general public. As public health concerns mounted, the market transitioned to single-use polyethylene bags giving birth to the ubiquitous 500ml ‘sachet water’ that now litters streets across Accra. Eventually, Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) bottles emerged as a symbol of elevated social status, alongside premium glass bottles for upmarket consumers. While sachets and PET bottles solved acute hygiene challenges, they birthed an unprecedented sanitation nightmare. Despite this trend, innovative corporate leaders in Accra are demonstrating that alternative models exist. Forward-thinking companies have begun distributing customized reusable water bottles to employees and installing universal water dispensers in corporate offices, drastically cutting down daily sachet and PET bottle consumption. The True Cost of Convenience: Environmental and Economic Toll The allure of single-use polystyrene lies in its immediate convenience and bargain. But the long-term trade-offs for Ghana’s economy and ecosystems are devastating. Every heavy rainstorm in Accra or Kumasi reveals the immediate impact: choked storm drains and gutters overflowing with white foam containers and plastic bags, triggering urban flooding and property damage. The underlying ecological crisis, however, is invisible to the naked eye. Neither plastic nor expanded polystyrene truly biodegrades. Under intense tropical ultraviolet radiation and physical stress, these materials fragment into microscopic particles—microplastics and nanoplastics. Furthermore, expanded polystyrene’s low density and high contamination rate make it economically unviable for traditional recycling systems. Local government assemblies bear the brunt of this burden, spending substantial portions of municipal budgets on manual cleanup and landfill management. The macroeconomic consequences extend far beyond waste collection: Agricultural Productivity: Littered farmlands suffer reduced soil aeration and crop yield, threatening rural livelihoods. Ecotourism Revenue: Plastic-strewn beaches along the Atlantic coastline degrade Ghana’s appeal to international travelers. Fisheries & Maritime Safety: Inland and coastal fishers report lost catch efficiency, damaged nets, and marine engine failures caused by plastic debris. Lessons from Abroad: Small Actions, National Impact Ghana is not alone in confronting single-use plastics. Across Europe, North America, and parts of Asia, retail ecosystems have implemented small financial disincentives—such as mandatory bag fees at supermarket checkouts—that effectively nudged consumers toward bringing their own tote bags. The power of individual action often spreads organically. A Ghanaian professional returning from an overseas family trip observed how international retailers discouraged single-use plastic. Inspired by the practice, his daughter began taking her own reusable tote bags for weekly grocery shopping back home in Accra. What started as a singular household habit soon caught the attention of friends. A Call for Behavioural Change: Reclaiming Our Heritage Policy regulations and government bans are vital, but policy alone cannot clean Ghana’s streets or protect its waterways. The January 1, 2027 EPA ban must serve as a catalyst for a deeper cultural and behavioral transformation. Achieving lasting sustainability requires every citizen, business owner, and community leader to rethink daily habits: Normalise Reusables: Proudly carry your own food containers, lunch boxes, and tote bags when buying food or groceries. Break the social stigma around reusable items. Support Green Vendors: Patronize street vendors and eateries that embrace leaf packaging, paper boxes, or reusable serveware. Adopt Corporate Responsibility: Businesses should eliminate single-use plastic bottles in boardrooms and staff canteens, providing universal water dispensers and branded reusable bottles. Educate the Next Generation: Teach children at home and in schools that true progress is measured by stewardship of our environment, not by disposable convenience. For decades, West African traditions exemplified sustainable living long before ‘going green’ became a global slogan. As Ghana prepares for the 2027 Styrofoam ban, the challenge before us is simple yet profound: to step forward into a cleaner future by stepping back into the wisdom of our roots. *** About the author: William Wallace Tamakloe is an Associate PR Director at Touchpoint Magna Carta.
