Votre mission : assurer le pilotage, la coordination et la supervision des activités financières, budgétaires et comptables, tout en contribuant à la fiabilité de l'information financière et au respect des procédures internes et de la réglementation en vigueur. VOS PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS Piloter le budget et la performance financière: coordonner l'élaboration du budget annuel, suivre son exécution, analyser les écarts et proposer les mesures correctives. Superviser la comptabilité: veiller à la bonne tenue de la comptabilité générale et, le cas échéant, analytique, à la justification des comptes, aux clôtures et à la préparation des états financiers. Sécuriser les dépenses: contrôler la conformité financière et documentaire des dossiers, la disponibilité budgétaire ainsi que le respect des procédures d'engagement et de paiement. Assurer le suivi de la trésorerie: superviser les recettes et dépenses, les rapprochements bancaires, les opérations de caisse et les prévisions de trésorerie. Coordonner le suivi financier de la paie travailler avec les ressources humaines sur les salaires, cotisations sociales, prélèvements fiscaux et autres éléments de rémunération. Contrôler les opérations d'achat: vérifier les factures et pièces justificatives et assurer le suivi financier des commandes avec les services concernés. Encadrer l'équipe: organiser et superviser le travail de l'équipe comptable et de caisse, répartir les tâches et veiller à l'application du contrôle interne. Produire le reporting: élaborer les tableaux de bord, rapports périodiques et analyses utiles à la prise de décision de la Direction Générale. Assurer les relations avec les partenaires externes: mettre à disposition les informations nécessaires aux audits, contrôles et travaux du Commissaire aux comptes. LE PROFIL QUE NOUS RECHERCHONS Formation être titulaire d'un diplôme de niveau BAC+3 minimum en Finance, Comptabilité, Gestion financière, Audit ou dans un domaine équivalent pertinent. Expérience: justifier d'au moins cinq (05) années d'expérience professionnelle pertinente en finance, comptabilité, contrôle financier ou gestion budgétaire, avec une expérience significative en supervision d'équipe ou en coordination d'activités financières et comptables. VOS COMPÉTENCES TECHNIQUES Bonne maîtrise des principes et normes comptables applicables, notamment du référentiel SYSCOHADA; Maîtrise de la gestion budgétaire, de l'analyse financière et du suivi de la trésorerie; Maîtrise des procédures de contrôle des dépenses, des engagements et des paiements; Bonne connaissance des obligations fiscales et sociales liées aux opérations financières et à la paie; Capacité à élaborer, analyser et présenter des états financiers, des tableaux de bord et des rapports de gestion; Bonne maîtrise des outils informatiques de gestion comptable et financière ainsi que des tableurs; Connaissance des dispositifs de contrôle interne, de gestion des risques financiers et de sécurisation des opérations; Maîtrise du système des SA. LES QUALITÉS QUI FERONT LA DIFFÉRENCE Rigueur et intégrité Sens élevé de la confidentialité Esprit d'analyse et de synthèse Leadership et aptitude à encadrer une équipe Organisation et gestion des priorités Autonomie et réactivité Force de proposition Excellentes capacités de communication et de collaboration Sens des responsabilités et orientation résultats. CONDITIONS DE CANDIDATURE Les candidat(e)s intéressé(e)s et répondant aux critères sont invité(e)s à constituer un dossier comprenant: Un curriculum vitae actualisé et détaillé; Une lettre de motivation adressée au Directeur Général de CFA-I; Les copies des diplômes et attestations pertinentes. Transmission des candidatures: les dossiers sont à envoyer à travers le lien : https://competenceforall.com/jobs/chef-de-service-finances-et-comptabilite-h-f-44 avec pour objet : « Candidature au poste de Chef(fe) de Service Finances et Comptabilité » . DATE LIMITE DE CANDIDATURE: 23 NOVEMBRE 2026 À 17 H Seul(e)s les candidat(e)s présélectionné(e)s seront contacté(e)s pour la suite du processus. Le Directeur Général Boureima GUIRO

items.title: Vice President urges stronger cybersecurity to protect mobile money users
items.description: Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has called for stronger data protection, cybersecurity and accountability in Ghana’s digital financial services sector to safeguard mobile money users against fraud and other risks. She said the rapid growth of mobile money and other digital financial services must be matched with reliable security systems to sustain public confidence in electronic transactions. Speaking at the MTN Ghana @30 Stakeholders Dinner in Accra, Professor Opoku-Agyemang acknowledged the role of mobile money in expanding financial inclusion, particularly for small businesses, families and people previously underserved by traditional banking services. She said the service had made it easier for businesses to receive payments and for families to transfer money across the country without relying on costly financial infrastructure. However, she warned that increasing dependence on digital platforms placed greater responsibility on service providers to protect customers. “Ghanaians who transact online are placing trust in our systems. That trust must be earned and defended through strong data protection, resilient cybersecurity, and clear accountability,” she said. The Vice President stressed that expanding access to mobile money should not be the ultimate goal of financial inclusion. She said users must also be able to access digital financial services safely and affordably, with adequate safeguards against fraud and other security threats. Professor Opoku-Agyemang disclosed that the government was developing a National Financial Inclusion and Development Strategy, which would place greater emphasis on consumer protection, financial well-being and ensuring that financial services meet the needs of individuals and businesses. She urged MTN Ghana to improve network quality and customer service while intensifying measures to protect subscribers against fraud. The Vice President also reaffirmed the government’s commitment to creating an enabling environment for investment in Ghana’s digital economy, while ensuring that the benefits of technological advancement are shared more widely.

items.title: With new speaker, Israel parliament moves to unravel Netanyahu legacy
items.description: Israel's parliament met under a new speaker from the anti-Benjamin Netanyahu bloc on Wednesday, as opponents of the caretaker prime minister began a legislative offensive to roll back his divisive legacy. In the vote for parliament speaker late on Tuesday, 66 lawmakers out of 120 voted in favour of Matan Kahana, an ally of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot who has until next month to form a government to replace Netanyahu.

items.title: US Saudi nuclear agreement 'satisfactory': IAEA
items.description: UN nuclear watchdog head Rafael Grossi on Wednesday welcomed a deal between the United States and Saudi Arabia on equipping the kingdom with a civilian nuclear programme. The deal announced in July has provoked questions about the risks of nuclear proliferation. "It's a very satisfactory outcome that we have with this agreement," Grossi told reporters after opening an International Atomic Energy Agency board of governors' meeting. Once nuclear power development gets under way in Saudi Arabia, "we will be there," he added.

2 Arabian gazelles born at King Salman Royal Natural Reserve
items.description: RIYADH: Two Arabian gazelles have been born at King Salman Royal Natural Reserve this month in a boost for the vulnerable species, the Saudi Press Agency reported on Tuesday. The births are part of the reserve’s ongoing program to reintroduce wildlife to boost biodiversity and restore ecological balance in the protected area. The Arabian gazelle is one of the species targeted by reintroduction programs. It is listed as vulnerable on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List.

items.title: Government allocates GH¢45m to expand rural telephony in 2027
items.description: Government has allocated GH¢45 million in the 2027 Budget to expand rural telephony and improve access to reliable and affordable telecommunications services in underserved communities, Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has announced. She said the investment forms part of efforts to bridge Ghana’s digital divide and ensure that communities outside major urban centres benefit from the country’s growing digital economy. Speaking at the MTN Ghana @30 Stakeholders Dinner in Accra, the Vice President stressed that access to technology should not depend on where a person lives. “Our priority is to extend reliable and affordable connectivity to communities that remain underserved, while upgrading existing infrastructure to support digital services,” she said. Professor Opoku-Agyemang said improved digital infrastructure would create opportunities for businesses, education, healthcare and the delivery of public services. The Vice President also highlighted the role of mobile money in expanding financial inclusion, particularly by enabling small businesses to receive payments and allowing families to transfer money conveniently across the country. She, however, cautioned that the growing reliance on digital financial services must be matched with stronger security measures to protect users. “Ghanaians who transact online are placing trust in our systems. That trust must be earned and defended through strong data protection, resilient cybersecurity, and clear accountability,” she stated. She said the next phase of financial inclusion should go beyond providing access to mobile money platforms to ensuring that users can access the services safely and affordably. Professor Opoku-Agyemang further disclosed that government was developing a National Financial Inclusion and Development Strategy, which would place greater emphasis on consumer protection, financial well-being and the needs of individuals and businesses. The Vice President urged MTN Ghana to increase investment in network quality, connectivity in underserved communities, customer service and measures to protect subscribers against fraud. “MTN, I therefore encourage you to invest even more in network quality, access to underserved communities, customer service and experience, and protection against fraud,” she said. She commended the telecommunications company for its contribution to Ghana’s digital economy over the past 30 years, citing its investments in infrastructure, employment and public revenue. She also acknowledged the work of the MTN Ghana Foundation in supporting initiatives in health, education and economic empowerment. Professor Opoku-Agyemang said government remained committed to creating an enabling environment for private sector investment while ensuring that the benefits of technological advancement were widely shared.

items.title: Senate forwards State Police Bill to Tinubu for assent
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA – The Senate has mandated the Clerk to the National Assembly, CNA, Kamoru Ogunlana to transmit the constitutional amendment bill that seeks to establish state police services in Nigeria to President Bola Tinubu for assent in line with the Acts Authentication Act, 2004. The Senate has urged President Tinubu to forward the National Policing Bill, which will provide for the operationalisation of subnational policing, to the National Assembly for legislative scrutiny and expeditious passage. In his remarks, the President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio said the executive is expected to send the modalities for the implementation of State Police Services to the National Assembly because they do not want to give unnecessary timelines, but time is of the essence. It is a bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services, and for Related Matters (Sixth Alteration) 2026. The bill, titled “A Bill for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 to Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services and for Related Matters,” seeks to create the constitutional framework for the establishment of state police across the federation. Resolutions of the Senate were sequel to a motion titled, “Passage of Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026” and sponsored by the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, APC, Ekiti Central. In his presentation, Senator Bamidele said, “The Senate: Recall that pursuant to Section 9(1) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999, the National Assembly, processed an Executive Bill seeking to alter the provisions of the Constitution to establish State Police as part of the national policing structure; “Also recall that the Senate and the House of Representatives on June 24th and July, 23rd 2026 respectively, overwhelmingly supported the Bill with over 2/3 majority votes, thereby meeting the Constitutional threshold for the passage of the Bill by the National Assembly; “Aware that the National Assembly transmitted the Bill to the 36 State Houses of Assembly for the mandatory approval by resolution of not less than 2/3 majority of the State Houses of Assembly as provided by Section 9(2) of the Constitution before the Bill can be passed; “Also, aware that the 36 State Houses of Assembly have transmitted their resolution the Bill to the National Assembly, namely: Abia, Adamawa, Anambra, Akwa-Ibom, Bauchi, Bayelsa, Benue, Borno, Cross-River, Delta, Ebonyi, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Gombe, Imo, Jigawa, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kebbi, Kogi, Kwara, Lagos, Nasarawa, Niger, Ogun, Ondo, Osun, Oyo, Plateau, Rivers, Sokoto, Taraba, Yobe and Zamfara; “Convinced that the Bill has fulfilled the conditions set out in Sections 9(1) and (2) of the Constitution for a Constitutional amendment of this nature to be passed.” Details later . Vanguard News The post Senate forwards State Police Bill to Tinubu for assent appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mahama targets 30% cross-border electricity trade in West Africa within five years
items.description: President John Mahama has called for greater investment in connecting national electricity grids across West Africa, saying it could raise cross-border power trade from the current 7 per cent to nearly 30 per cent within five years. He said stronger connections between countries would enable nations with surplus electricity to supply others, which will help to lower power costs and provide the reliable energy needed to support industrial growth. The President said this while addressing the West Africa Integration and Investment Summit in Sierra Leone on Wednesday, November 18. President Mahama said countries in the region must move away from relying solely on their individual electricity generation capacity and instead take advantage of opportunities to share power. “We do not all have to build hydro dams. We do not all have to build gas plants. We do not all have to build power plants. We can exchange electricity amongst ourselves at tariffs that are affordable,” he said. He disclosed that electricity traded through the West African Power Pool currently accounts for about 7 per cent of the region’s electricity market. President Mahama said Ghana’s expanding gas resources and investments in thermal power generation could position the country to supply about 2,000 megawatts of surplus electricity to the regional market. However, he identified inadequate interconnections between national electricity grids as a major obstacle to making such exchanges possible. He said countries could generate surplus electricity but would struggle to supply it to neighbouring markets without the necessary transmission infrastructure. “If we have excess power, 2,000 megawatts, put it on the West African Power Pool. But the problem is if you put it on, where are you going to evacuate it to if you are not connected?” he asked. The President said strengthening regional electricity trade would be important to West Africa’s industrialisation ambitions, noting that businesses require affordable energy to operate and expand. “You cannot industrialise when you do not have affordable power,” he maintained.

items.title: Local organic fertiliser offers farmers a pathway to climate-resilient agriculture
items.description: When the rains failed to come as expected, Isaiah Yahaya Moses watched his soybean plants wilt and change colour. The leaves had begun to lose their green appearance, a worrying sign for a farmer whose livelihood depends on the success of each growing season. In the Northern Region of Ghana, where many farmers depend on rainfall for crop production, an unreliable rainy season can translate into lost income, mounting production costs and difficulty sustaining the next farming season. Isaiah had experienced the consequences before. His soybean harvest had generally remained below 15 bags in previous years. “We were not getting enough rainfall, and the soybean leaves began to change colour. In previous years, I harvested about 15 bags or fewer,” he says. After applying Organic Farming Aid (OFA), a local agricultural product promoted by HGA Africa, he noticed a change in the appearance of his crops. The leaves became greener, and he eventually harvested 30 bags from the five acres on which he used the product. “After applying the product, I realised that the whole thing had changed into green. Just seeing it alone will tell you that the product was good,” he says. For Isaiah, the harvest represented relief after previous seasons of disappointing yields. His is not the only account coming from some farming communities in Ghana. At Ayenasu in the Ejura Sekyeredumase Municipality of the Ashanti Region, maize farmer Frimpong Manso has struggled with difficult soil conditions since he began cultivating the land in 2017. The high concentration of stones in his farmland, coupled with unpredictable rainfall, has made farming increasingly challenging. He relied on conventional fertilisers, including NPK and urea, but says the results did not justify the expenditure. “I applied fertilisers, but I wasn’t getting the expected yield. The erratic rainfall patterns in the country have also added to the difficulty,” he says. After adopting OFA, he noticed improvements in the development of his maize crops, even during a period when rainfall was insufficient. He had initially projected a harvest of 20 bags from his three-acre farm but became more optimistic after observing the crop’s growth. For Frimpong, the prospect of a better harvest also offers the possibility of reducing expenditure on farm inputs. In Konongo, garden egg farmers Musah Zakari, Solomon Tettey and Amina Braimah describe similar pressures. They say previous farming seasons were affected by poor weather conditions, fruit abortion and pest infestations. The cost of fertiliser added to their difficulties. They recall spending about GH¢500 on a bag of fertiliser and purchasing two bags without achieving the results they had expected. Musah says the growth of their crops has improved since they began using OFA. “Our garden looks so green and healthy. We’re expecting a bumper harvest,” he says. For 64-year-old Samuel Frimpong, who has cultivated plantain on a 70-hectare farm at Agogo since 2002, the challenge has also been about the rising cost of keeping a farm productive. Fertiliser, chemicals and labour have placed considerable pressure on his operations. During dry periods, he sometimes spends as much as GH¢500 a day on additional labour to water his crops. He says the financial burden makes it difficult to sustain production. Since adopting OFA, Samuel reports improvements in his harvests. On his watermelon farm, he says production increased from approximately 4,000 fruits to 8,000. He also reports an increase in the number of Kia truckloads harvested, from one to as many as four. How soil health connects to climate resilience The challenges described by these farmers are closely linked to the vulnerability of rain-fed agriculture to climate variability. Experts say when rainfall is delayed, becomes erratic or stops for extended periods, crops can experience water stress. The effects depend on the crop, its growth stage, soil characteristics and the duration of the dry spell. Dr Benjamin Aboagye Danso, a Crop Scientist at the University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development (USTED), explains that soil organic matter is important in determining how effectively farmland captures and retains rainfall. Organic matter contributes to soil structure by helping bind soil particles into aggregates. This supports the formation of pores that allow water to infiltrate and remain within the root zone. He explains that well-structured soils with sufficient organic matter can retain more plant-available water, providing crops with a buffer between rainfall events. Not all water entering the soil, however, he says, is available to plants, adding that, some drains beyond the reach of roots, while some is held so tightly by soil particles that crops cannot readily extract it. For farmers facing irregular rainfall, the amount of water retained in the soil and available to crops can therefore influence how long plants maintain growth during dry spells. Dr Danso also highlights the importance of soil management practices in maintaining organic matter and improving moisture retention. These include retaining crop residues as mulch, applying locally available organic materials such as composted crop waste and manure, practising conservation tillage, and incorporating suitable leguminous cover crops into farming systems. Such practices can help protect the soil surface, reduce moisture loss and improve soil structure over time. Their effectiveness, however, depends on local soil conditions, the type of organic material used and how the practices are implemented. He states that, the relationship between soil health and crop resilience also has physical limits, indicating that even a well-structured soil with good organic matter content cannot supply water indefinitely when rainfall remains insufficient. During prolonged drought, stored soil moisture can eventually become depleted. Compacted subsoil layers can also restrict root penetration, limiting crops’ access to water deeper underground. According to him, high temperatures can further increase the rate at which crops lose water. And when atmospheric demand exceeds the capacity of the soil-root system to supply moisture, plants may close their stomata to conserve water, restricting photosynthesis and potentially reducing yields. “This means that improving soil health can strengthen the capacity of farming systems to cope with some rainfall variability, but it cannot replace other adaptation measures such as supplemental irrigation where feasible, drought-tolerant crop varieties, appropriate planting calendars and effective water management,” he emphasized. It is within this broader relationship between soil health, water availability and crop development that the potential contribution of OFA is being discussed. Produced by HGA Africa, Organic Farming Aid is promoted as a liquid organic fertiliser intended to support crop development and soil health. The potential of the product to contribute to climate adaptation was discussed at the fourth annual HGA Africa Forum in Tamale, where farmers shared experiences and considered the relationship between crop drought resilience and farm profitability. Chief Agronomist of HGA Africa, Gilbert Osei, says the product’s potential contribution to climate adaptation is linked to root development and the effective utilisation of soil moisture and nutrients. He explains that well-established root systems can help plants access moisture from deeper soil layers when surface moisture becomes limited. He also indicates that reducing the time crops take to mature could limit their exposure to prolonged periods of moisture stress. “Once these root systems are well established, in case there is the presence of droughts, the root systems of the plants are able to seek further moisture on their own,” he says. What agricultural field trials reveal Farmers’ experiences offer useful accounts of how OFA is being applied, but agricultural field trials provide another perspective on its potential effectiveness. A report published by the UK-Ghana Chamber of Commerce on 10 October 2024 includes a summary of field trials involving different crops and soil conditions. The report identifies researchers from the University of Ghana and the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research’s Savanna Agricultural Research Institute (CSIR-SARI), among others, as contributors to the trials. One study on cowpea conducted on poor soils near Tamale by Dr Edwin Korbla Akley and colleagues at CSIR-SARI recorded a 55 per cent increase in yield following the application of OFA compared with an untreated control. The reported crop profit margin also increased from 27 per cent to 124 per cent. The trial is identified in the report as having been published in the journal Agronomy . Another study on maize near Tamale, attributed to Dr Ophelia Asirifi Amoako of CSIR-SARI, examined the use of OFA alongside inorganic fertiliser. The findings indicated that applying OFA as a booster with 50 per cent of the standard quantity of inorganic fertiliser produced yields similar to those obtained using the full standard quantity. The report says this approach could save farmers almost half of their fertiliser costs. The study is identified as having been published in the American Journal of Plant Sciences. Other reported trials provide additional findings. On irrigated rice farms near Kpong, a trial summary indicated that OFA alone increased yields by 37 per cent and profits by 53 per cent compared with an untreated control. Inorganic fertiliser increased yields by 43 per cent but profits by only four per cent. The strongest reported outcome came from combining OFA with half the usual quantity of inorganic fertiliser, which increased yields by 67 per cent and profits by 75 per cent. A maize trial near Legon recorded a 41 per cent yield increase with OFA compared with an untreated control, while inorganic fertiliser produced a 30 per cent increase. Another maize trial near Kpong reported a 102 per cent yield increase with OFA compared with an untreated control affected by fall armyworm. The economic case for sustainable farming The experiences of the farmers also highlight an important consideration in climate adaptation that, agricultural interventions must make economic sense if farmers are to continue using them. For farmers such as Samuel, the cost of watering crops during dry periods can be substantial. For Frimpong and the Konongo garden egg farmers, the cost of fertiliser and the uncertainty of getting a worthwhile harvest influence decisions about what to apply to their farms. HGA Africa’s Chief Executive Officer, Herring Abraham, says environmental sustainability must be accompanied by improved farm profitability if farmers are to embrace greener agricultural practices. “Telling farmers to make farming greener and lose money is not a good message. It’s not going to be an effective message,” he says. He believes interventions that combine environmental considerations with improved productivity could encourage wider adoption of sustainable farming practices. For policymakers, this points to the importance of considering the financial realities of farmers when designing climate adaptation programmes. The cost of an intervention, its availability, the suitability of the product for local soil and crop conditions, and the consistency of its results all influence whether farmers can adopt it over time. HGA Africa’s Chief Executive Officer estimates that OFA contributed approximately US$20 million in increased farmer incomes in 2024. A possible pathway, not a single solution Ghana’s agricultural resilience will require improved soil health, stronger access to appropriate agricultural technologies, efficient water management and better access to climate information. OFA represents one approach being adopted by farmers who say they are experiencing improvements in crop development and harvests. The field-trial summaries also report potential yield and economic benefits in some crop and soil conditions, including where the product is used alongside reduced quantities of conventional fertiliser. For farmers such as Isaiah, Frimpong and Samuel, their concerns are whether the next farming season will deliver better results and allow them to sustain their livelihoods. Their experiences offer a starting point for understanding how agricultural interventions could contribute to climate adaptation. As Ghana confronts the combined pressures of climate change and food insecurity, experts say the challenge is not just to introduce more agricultural products. It is to identify, test and scale solutions that deliver measurable improvements in farmers’ lives. For now, OFA is offering some farmers renewed optimism. Whether its reported benefits can be consistently reproduced across Ghana’s diverse agricultural landscapes will be an important measure of its contribution to a more climate-resilient food system.

items.title: Photos: MTN Ghana marks 30 years of service with stakeholder dinner
items.description: Telecommunications giant MTN Ghana has marked its 30th anniversary with a stakeholder dinner in Accra, celebrating three decades of connecting people, businesses and communities and contributing to Ghana’s digital and socio-economic development. The event, held under the theme, “ 30 Years of Progress, Powered by You ,” was attended by Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang, the Sempe Akweiman Mantse, Nii Adote Odaawulu I, who represented the Ga Mantse, King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, and several ministers of state and heads of regulatory institutions. Also present were MTN Group Board Chairman, Mcebisi Jonas; MTN Group President and CEO, Ralph Mupita; members of the Group Executive Committee; the Chairman of the MTN Ghana Board, Ishmael Yamson; and MTN Ghana CEO, Stephen Blewett. Chief executives of public and private institutions, directors and management of MTN Ghana and its subsidiaries, media representatives and civil society organisations also joined the celebration. Speaking at the event, MTN Ghana Chief Executive Officer Stephen Blewett thanked Ghanaians for their trust and support over the past 30 years, saying the company’s growth had been shaped by its relationship with the country. He traced MTN’s journey from its beginnings as Spacefon in 1996 through key milestones, including the establishment of the MTN Ghana Foundation in 2007, the introduction of Mobile Money in 2009 and its listing on the Ghana Stock Exchange in 2018. Mr Blewett said MTN now serves more than 32 million subscribers and plans to invest US$1.1 billion over the next three years, alongside the rollout of 500 new cell sites this year. He reaffirmed the company’s commitment to expanding digital access, improving network reliability and supporting Ghana’s socio-economic development. In his remarks, MTN Ghana Board Chairman, Ishmael Yamson, said the company’s legacy should be measured not only by its infrastructure, market share and financial performance but also by its contribution to society. He said MTN’s growth from a telecommunications provider into a company supporting financial inclusion, education and community development demonstrated its commitment to being a “force for good”. Mr Yamson reaffirmed the Board’s commitment to responsible corporate governance, integrity and safeguarding the trust Ghanaians have placed in the company.

items.title: Ghana Energy Awards’ EPOP extends reach close to 16,000 students nationwide
items.description: The Ghana Energy Awards (GEA), through its flagship Energy Personality Outreach Programme (EPOP), has extended its reach to close to 16,000 students nationwide, following its latest engagement with over 700 students from three schools in the Western Region. The 2026 Western Region edition of the programme, held on Tuesday, 17 th November 2026, at St. John’s Senior High School, combined career inspiration and industry engagement with practical interventions under the Ghana Energy Awards’ 10th Anniversary Legacy Initiative, aimed at strengthening educational infrastructure and improving conditions for learning in the beneficiary schools. Held under the theme, “Impacting the Next Generation Leaders Today,” the programme brought together students from St. John’s Senior High School, Sekondi College and Kikam Technical Institute. They engaged with the 2025 Energy Personalities of the Year: Madam Judith Adjobah Blay, Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana National Gas Limited Company (Ghana Gas), and Mr. Edward E. Obeng-Kenzo, Chief Executive of the Volta River Authority (VRA). As part of the GEA 10th Anniversary Legacy Initiative, each of the three beneficiary schools received 50 bunk beds and 50 streetlights. The provision of the bunk beds was made possible through the support of the VRA and the Ghana Gas, while the streetlights were provided through the generous of the Ministry of Energy and Green Transition. The bunk beds are intended to improve student accommodation and create a more comfortable and conducive boarding environment, while the streetlights will enhance illumination and visibility across the school premises, strengthen safety and contribute to a more secure environment for students and the wider school community. Investing in the Next Generation Addressing the gathering, Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Energy Awards, Rev. Ing. Henry Teinor, underscored the importance of deliberately investing in young people to secure the future of Ghana’s energy sector. He explained that EPOP was established by the Energy Media Group, organisers of the prestigious Ghana Energy Awards, to bridge the knowledge gap between students and the energy industry, expose young people to career opportunities and inspire them to acquire the knowledge, education and skills required to contribute meaningfully to the sector. He noted that, over the years, the programme has engaged more than 15,000 students across Ghana, reaching second-cycle institutions as well as technical and vocational education and training institutions. Rev. Ing. Teinor explained that the inclusion of the outreach programme in the Ghana Energy Awards’ 10 th Anniversary celebrations reflects the organisation’s determination to build a legacy that extends beyond the annual recognition of excellence in the energy sector. He said the Legacy Initiative was conceived to translate the Awards’ milestone celebration into tangible interventions that support education and contribute to the development of the next generation. The support provided to the three schools, he noted, demonstrates the value of collaboration between sector institutions and the education sector in creating opportunities for young people. Ghana Gas CEO Announces Annual Scholarships A major highlight of Madam Judith Adjobah Blay’s engagement with the students was her announcement that Ghana Gas would provide five scholarships annually for outstanding students from each of the three participating schools. She also proposed a partnership with the schools to establish or strengthen career counselling and mentorship programmes to help students make informed academic and professional choices. In further support of their development, she donated books on leadership, personal development and positive attitudes to encourage learning and personal growth. Speaking on purpose, finding one’s voice and creating a path to success, Madam Blay encouraged the students to recognise that opportunities in the energy sector extend far beyond engineering and the sciences. Drawing on her professional experience across procurement, banking, policymaking and local content, she demonstrated how individuals from diverse professional backgrounds contribute to the effective functioning of the energy sector. She identified opportunities in fields such as accounting, law, environmental management, administration, and health and safety. She urged the students to identify and develop their talents, embrace emerging technologies and cultivate the values of discipline, integrity, punctuality, teamwork and continuous learning. Leadership and Direct Engagement Ing. Edward Ekow Obeng-Kenzo encouraged the students to understand leadership as a responsibility anchored in service, continuous learning and sound decision-making. He emphasised the importance of reading, personal development, mentorship and building positive relationships, urging the students to remain curious, share knowledge and use their abilities to contribute to the growth of others. Interactive Session with Students The programme also featured an interactive question-and-answer session, during which students from the three schools engaged directly with the two Energy Personalities on career choices, leadership, professional development and opportunities within the energy sector. The session provided an opportunity for the students to draw practical lessons from the executives’ professional journeys, ask questions about the sector and gain valuable guidance on preparing for their future careers. Now in its eighth year, EPOP has engaged students across several senior high schools and educational institutions, including Achimota Senior High School, West Africa Senior High School, St. Mary’s Senior High School, Nungua Senior High School, Aburi Girls’ Senior High School, Wesley Grammar School and Chemu Senior High School. A Decade of Redefining Excellence As the Ghana Energy Awards celebrates its 10 th anniversary, the Western Region edition of EPOP demonstrates the Awards Secretariat’s commitment to ensuring that the impact of the Awards extends well beyond the recognition of excellence. Having reached close to 16,000 students nationwide, EPOP continues to serve as a vital platform for deepening awareness of the energy sector, inspiring career aspirations and equipping young people with the knowledge and motivation to become the next generation of industry leaders.

items.title: Bawumia meets film industry stakeholders; calls for tax incentives, streaming platform
items.description: Former Vice-President and New Patriotic Party (NPP) flag bearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has called for tax incentives for filmmakers, increased government investment and a dedicated streaming platform to support Ghana’s film industry. He said Ghana had failed to recognise the economic potential of the creative arts, particularly the film sector, despite its capacity to create jobs and generate revenue. Dr Bawumia made the remarks in a Facebook post following a meeting with representatives of Ghana’s film industry as part of his stakeholder engagements. He said the industry players highlighted several challenges confronting the sector, including unfair competition from foreign films, inadequate cinema screens, limited training facilities and the high cost of production. “My message to them was simple. Ghana has not appreciated the economic potential of the creative arts, especially film. The job creation potential is huge, but successive governments have only paid lip service to it,” he wrote. To address the challenges, the former Vice-President called for the passage of the Broadcasting Act, the introduction of tax incentives for filmmakers and the establishment of a dedicated streaming platform for Ghanaian films. He also stressed the need for government investment in the sector through partnerships with private businesses, describing such support as an economic necessity rather than a favour. “Government investment, in partnership with the private sector, is not a favour. It is an economic necessity,” he said. Dr Bawumia maintained that Ghana had the talent and stories to build a strong film industry but lacked the political will to provide the necessary support. “Ghana has the talent. Ghana has the stories. What has been missing is the will to back them,” he added. The proposals echo some of the commitments the NPP made to the creative arts, tourism and culture sectors in its 2024 manifesto, which was launched in Takoradi on Sunday, 18 August 2024. The party pledged to use tax incentives, including a flat tax, to encourage private sector investment in tourism and creative arts facilities. It also promised to establish, in partnership with the private sector, a streaming and digital management platform for Ghanaian content developers, alongside a Travel Protocol Service to support creatives undertaking international engagements.

items.title: Ghana pushes for increased investment in child protection at Manila conference
items.description: Ghana has called for increased investment in child protection systems and stronger institutions to help end violence against children, as the country joins global leaders at the Second Global Ministerial Conference on Ending Violence Against Children in Manila, Philippines. The Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, is leading Ghana’s delegation to the conference, which brings together governments and development partners to assess progress and discuss practical strategies for preventing violence against children. Ahead of the main conference, Dr Lartey participated in a high-level satellite event on the theme, “Strengthening Child Protection Systems and Financing for Sustainable Impact.” The event, co-hosted by Save the Children, UNICEF and World Vision International, brought together ministers, development partners, civil society organisations and international financial institutions to examine sustainable ways of financing child protection services. Addressing the gathering, Dr Lartey said ending violence against children required more than policy commitments, emphasising the need for strong institutions, adequately resourced social services and sustained domestic financing. She called for child protection to be treated as an essential public service, just like health and education, with dedicated and protected budgetary allocations. Highlighting Ghana’s efforts, the Minister recalled that the country became the first in the world to ratify the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child in 1990. She also pointed to the Children’s Act, 1998 (Act 560), as part of the country’s legal framework for protecting children. Dr Lartey further highlighted the nationwide reach of the Integrated Social Services initiative, which now operates in all 261 districts to improve coordination, referrals and the early identification of risks affecting children. She said the government was also working to strengthen the social service workforce, improve financing and enhance accountability, with plans to introduce dedicated child protection budget lines across all 261 districts by 2028. The Minister urged governments, development partners and international financial institutions to increase funding for child protection, stressing that partnerships should reinforce national systems rather than establish parallel structures. She cited Ghana’s Child Labour Public-Private Partnership as an example of collaboration aimed at protecting children working in high-risk sectors. Dr Lartey reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to ending violence against children, calling for global commitments to be supported by practical action, effective institutions and sustainable financing. She also said Ghana would use President John Dramani Mahama’s forthcoming chairmanship of the African Union in 2027 to maintain continental focus on child protection. The conference provides Ghana with an opportunity to share its experiences, learn from other countries and strengthen partnerships towards building a more effective and responsive child protection system.

items.title: Putin-Trump-Xi: Three men, three different agendas
items.description: An unprecedented trilateral summit of the leaders of China, Russia and the US will provide startling images and unsettle Europe this week, but all three presidents are approaching the meeting with starkly different agendas. Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will meet Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen for talks that have echoes of the US-UK-USSR February 1945 “big three” summit in Yalta. At that meeting, which took place months before the end of World War II, the leaders of Britain, the Soviet Union and the US agreed the postwar division of Europe. Europe, which will not have a representative at Thursday’s talks, will be eyeing them warily. The smiles and friendly handshakes may also cause chills in Ukraine, after almost half a decade of war with Russia, and Taiwan, the democratic island viewed by China as part of its territory. But analysts say it is unlikely that the meeting will result in a landmark breakthrough on key issues such as Ukraine, nuclear disarmament and AI, even if the fact it is taking place at all is remarkable. Here AFP looks at what the three men will want from the meeting. Putin: imagery and Ukraine On paper, Putin will be in the meeting as the junior partner, presiding over a country whose population, let alone economy, is dwarfed by both the United States and China. But the war sparked by Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine, which Trump famously vowed to resolve in 24 hours, will be at the centre of the talks as the conflict grinds towards its fifth anniversary. Putin will be buoyed by being able to set out his conditions for ending the war without Kyiv’s chief allies, the Europeans, or Ukraine being at the table. “He wants Russia, the US and China to decide everyone else’s geopolitical fate. But in the end it’s impossible to decide on the fundamentals of European security without Europeans,” said Fredrik Wesslau, senior policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR). The optics of the meeting, set to be relayed extensively by Russia’s state-controlled media, are also very important for Putin who has always pressed for Moscow to be seen as a great global power even after the collapse of the USSR. “A seat alongside the American and Chinese presidents would affirm Russia’s status as a global power, despite its much weaker economic position,” said Tsiporah Fried, senior fellow at the Hudson Institute. “Political rehabilitation would be a gain even without concessions on territory, sanctions, or Ukraine’s future alignment,” she added. Trump: nuclear and overcoming midterms Trump and the White House have framed the trilateral summit as a way of advancing nuclear arms control, although the president himself admitted before leaving Washington “it’s a tough subject because it’s very hard for any of us to say we’ll get rid of our nukes.” The imagery is also important for Trump as the 80-year-old contemplates his last two years in office as a lame-duck president following his Republican Party’s brutal defeat in the US midterm elections earlier this month. Opponents also accuse Trump of having little to show for the hugely costly war against Iran, although the president insisted “we have Iran in very good shape.” In an early win for Trump, Xi took the unusual step of personally greeting him on arrival in Shenzhen. “Typically after bad midterms, this is how presidents reset and remind other leaders that they’re still in charge on foreign policy,” said Edgard Kagan, senior adviser at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS). Trump will be wary of suggesting any easing of the restrictions on the export to China of the technology that powers AI, with the summit coming on the heels of the resignation of Jensen Huang, chief executive of AI chip giant Nvidia, over an affair with an alleged Chinese agent. “The room for manoeuvre for the Americans is constrained by the Nvidia scandal,” said Mathilde Velliet, a researcher at the French Institute of International Relations (IFRI), saying it had already led to a “hardening” of the US stance. China: glory for host, Taiwan and stability As host, Xi knows “the meeting could place China at the centre of global diplomacy and reinforce its standing alongside the United States,” said Fried, while cautioning “Beijing has reasons to avoid an ambitious agenda”. Beijing has maintained a careful stance throughout the Ukraine war, staying officially neutral while rejecting accusations of offering more than just tacit support to Russia including the alleged export of dual-use technology. “Xi does not want Russia to lose since this would be an overall win for the West,” said Wesslau. Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Mao Ning described the summit as being of “groundbreaking significance” with the three men due to have an “in-depth exchange of views on safeguarding world peace and enabling strategic stability in major-country relations.” On the nuclear issue, “China prefers bilateral nuclear talks with the United States over a trilateral format involving Russia,” said Tong Zhao, senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment, saying this allows Beijing to exercise leverage on matters it regards as “higher-priority” issues such as US arms sales to Taiwan. Vanguard News The post Putin-Trump-Xi: Three men, three different agendas appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Axe Kankan–Siguiri : quatre morts et un blessé dans un grave accident à Nourako
items.description: Un grave accident de la circulation a endeuillé l'axe Kankan–Siguiri dans la matinée de ce mercredi. Le drame s'est produit à hauteur de Nourako, entre Forécariah-Balimana et le district de Dalaba. Le bilan provisoire fait état de quatre morts et d'un blessé, selon les témoignages recueillis sur place. D'après les premières informations rapportées par des témoins, l'accident serait survenu à la suite d'une collision impliquant deux camions, dont l'un était immobilisé après une panne. Après le choc, le véhicule transportant les victimes aurait terminé sa course contre un arbre de néré. Les quatre occupants auraient perdu la vie sur place, tandis qu'un autre passager a été blessé et évacué vers Kankan pour recevoir des soins. Des proches sous le choc La violence du choc et l'état du véhicule témoignent de la gravité de l'accident. Sur les lieux, proches des victimes et habitants de la localité étaient sous le choc. Madou Traoré, frère de l'une des personnes décédées, raconte avoir appris la nouvelle à la suite d'un appel téléphonique reçu par un ami de son frère. « C'est mon frère qui est décédé aujourd'hui. Un de ses amis l'a appelé pour lui demander de l'argent. C'est finalement une autre personne qui a décroché le téléphone pour informer son ami qu'il avait été victime d'un grave accident. Je suis venu constater les faits et, comme vous pouvez le voir, l'état du véhicule est très alarmant. Un camion était tombé en panne sur la route et c'est ce véhicule qui aurait été percuté. Quatre personnes ont perdu la vie sur place », témoigne-t-il, encore sous le choc. Un autre témoin explique : « Ce matin, un ami m'a appelé pour m'informer qu'un accident s'était produit ici. Je suis venu et j'ai effectivement constaté qu'il y avait quatre morts. Selon les premières informations, deux camions se sont heurtés. L'un s'est retrouvé d'un côté de la route et l'autre de l'autre côté. Un véhicule qui venait de Siguiri, aux environs de 6 heures, a ensuite percuté le camion avant de terminer sa course contre un arbre de néré. Les quatre personnes qui se trouvaient à bord sont décédées et une autre personne a été blessée, puis évacuée à Kankan. » Il précise également que les agents de la gendarmerie ont procédé au constat avant de remettre les corps aux équipes de la Croix-Rouge, qui les ont transportés à la morgue de Siguiri dans une ambulance. Deux camions impliqués Un autre habitant de Forécariah-Balimana, Kaba Doumbouya, confirme les faits et décrit la scène à laquelle il a assisté après avoir été alerté par des habitants. « Nous étions en ville lorsque des personnes sont venues nous informer qu'un accident s'était produit ici, à Nourako. Nous sommes immédiatement venus sur les lieux. Deux camions étaient impliqués dans l'accident. L'un était renversé sur le côté droit et l'autre se trouvait sur la chaussée. Le véhicule qui venait de Siguiri a percuté l'un des camions avant de finir sa course contre un arbre de néré. Malheureusement, les occupants ont perdu la vie », raconte-t-il. À la suite du drame, les services de la gendarmerie et les équipes de la Croix-Rouge se sont mobilisés pour les opérations de constatation et de prise en charge des victimes. Les quatre corps ont été transférés à la morgue de Siguiri. En attendant les conclusions des autorités compétentes sur les circonstances exactes de cet accident, ce nouveau drame relance la question de la sécurité routière sur cet axe très fréquenté de la région de Kankan. Karifa Kansan Doumbouya correspondant régional à Kankan L’article Axe Kankan–Siguiri : quatre morts et un blessé dans un grave accident à Nourako est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Mbour : 79 kg de chanvre indien saisis, deux chauffeurs de taxi déférés au parquet
items.description: La Sûreté urbaine du commissariat central de Mbour a saisi 79 kilogrammes de chanvre indien et interpellé deux hommes, le 14 novembre, selon un communiqué de la Police nationale publié ce mercredi. Les suspects, chauffeurs de taxi, ont été déférés devant le procureur de la République le 16 novembre. Tout commence par une patrouille dans le quartier ONCAD. Les policiers repèrent un véhicule au comportement suspect et le suivent jusqu'au pont du quartier, où ils l'immobilisent. Le conducteur prend alors la fuite, abandonnant la voiture et son téléphone. Dans le véhicule, les enquêteurs découvrent trois sacs contenant le chanvre, recouverts de plastique. Un piège tendu par téléphone Le téléphone du fuyard sonne sans arrêt. Les policiers décrochent et comprennent qu'il s'agit du destinataire de la marchandise. Se faisant passer pour le chauffeur, ils lui donnent rendez-vous au pont de l'ONCAD pour la livraison. Deux hommes se présentent pour récupérer le colis et sont immédiatement interpellés, précise la police. L'exploitation de leurs téléphones aurait ensuite établi qu'ils étaient en contact régulier avec le conducteur en fuite. Placés en garde à vue, ils sont poursuivis pour détention, offre et cession de chanvre indien. O.B.N

items.title: Supreme Court reserves judgment in Zamfara North APC senatorial dispute
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Supreme Court on Wednesday reserved judgment in the legal dispute concerning the All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election for the Zamfara North Senatorial District, ahead of the 2027 general elections. A five-member panel of the court, led by Justice Tijani Abubakar, reserved the matter for judgment after the contending parties adopted their respective briefs of argument. The appeal, marked SC/CV/840/2026, was lodged before the apex court by Senator Sahabi Ya’u, who is seeking to set aside a verdict the Sokoto Division of the Court of Appeal delivered in the matter. The APC had declared that Senator Ya’u won a primary election it conducted in the senatorial district on May 19. However, dissatisfied with the outcome of the primary, a governorship aspirant of the party, Dr. Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi, took the matter to court. While challenging the process that led to the emergence of Senator Ya’u as the party’s flag bearer, Shinkafi told the court that no valid primary was conducted in the senatorial district. Processes before the court showed that the party had cleared three aspirants, Hanafi Musa Moriki, Shinkafi and Ya’u, to contest the primary poll. Shinkafi, in his suit, maintained that, contrary to the APC’s position, no valid consensus was reached among the aspirants to warrant the nomination of Senator Ya’u as the unopposed candidate. He told the court that he neither withdrew nor endorsed anyone as a consensus nominee, adding that he did not submit any written consent to withdraw from the race. Cited as respondents in the matter were the APC, INEC and Senator Ya’u. Meanwhile, in a judgment delivered on August 31, Justice Hassan Dikko of the Federal High Court in Gusau, Zamfara State, nullified the primary poll and ordered the APC to conduct a fresh one within 14 days. The high court held that the action of the APC was not in tandem with the principle of internal democracy entrenched in the party’s Constitution. Dissatisfied with the judgment, Senator Ya’u lodged an appeal before the Sokoto Division of the Court of Appeal. He, among other things, challenged the jurisdiction of the high court to meddle in a matter he said was within the realm of the domestic affairs of a political party and therefore non-justiciable. However, the appeal was dismissed, as the appellate court upheld the high court’s decision in the matter. Not happy with the verdict, Senator Ya’u approached the Supreme Court to set aside the concurrent decisions of the two lower courts. While the appellant argued his case on Wednesday through a team of lawyers led by Mr. Wale Balogun, SAN, the 1st respondent, Dr. Shinkafi, was represented by Mr. Bello Galadi, who filed a brief of argument on November 13 urging the court to dismiss the appeal for want of merit. INEC’s counsel, Mr. M.T. Abubakar, said the commission did not file any process in the matter. The Justice Abubakar-led panel said it would communicate the judgment date to all the parties. The post Supreme Court reserves judgment in Zamfara North APC senatorial dispute appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Diasporas africaines : des journalistes formés pour raconter autrement la migration
items.description: Treize journalistes du Sénégal, du Maroc et de la Côte d'Ivoire sont réunis depuis lundi à Rabat. Ils participent au lancement de « Voix et perspectives des diasporas », la composante médias du projet Pomire Sud-Sud, cofinancé par l'Union européenne et le ministère allemand du Développement. Sami Badreddine, chef du projet Pomire à la DW Akademie, a décliné l’objectif. Il s'agit de « promouvoir une perception équilibrée et inclusive de la migration », en valorisant les réussites des diasporas et des récits médiatiques documentés. Concrètement, le projet veut permettre aux diasporas installées au Maroc, en Côte d'Ivoire et au Sénégal de partager leurs réussites, de renforcer le réseautage Sud-Sud et de contribuer au développement local. Pour lui, l'originalité tient à la géographie. « D'habitude, quand on parle des diasporas, c'est souvent une diaspora qui se trouve dans un pays du Nord. » Cette fois, l'accent est mis sur les mobilités entre pays du Sud. Anta Seck, journaliste à la RTS, veut dépasser le récit de l'immigration irrégulière. « Comment raconter aujourd'hui la diaspora sénégalaise ? En quoi peut-elle participer à l'économie des pays, sans parler forcément que de transferts d'argent ? » Pierre Dipomelin, de la Nouvelle chaîne ivoirienne (NCI), veut mettre en lumière les migrants légaux qui contribuent à l'économie de leur pays d'accueil et l'enrichissent culturellement. Selon lui, les journalistes doivent « apprendre à changer de discours ». Le Sénégal fait partie des six pays du projet, avec la Côte d'Ivoire, la Guinée, le Mali, le Maroc et la Tunisie. Doté de 5,8 millions d'euros sur trois ans, Pomire Sud-Sud vise trois objectifs, rappelle Léo Julien Pagnac, chef du projet à la GIZ Maroc à savoir « renforcer les liens entre institutions, améliorer l’emploi et l'entrepreneuriat des diasporas, et mieux informer sur leur présence. C’est pour ça que nous sommes là aujourd'hui », souligne-t-il. Els Mortier, cheffe d'équipe « Migration et résilience » à la Délégation de l'UE en Côte d'Ivoire, attend des participants « des contenus qui donneront une image positive de la diaspora ». Des représentants du département chargé des Marocains résidant à l'étranger et de la société civile ont aussi assisté à l'ouverture. L'atelier, animé par les formateurs de la DW Akademie, se poursuit jusqu'à vendredi. Abdou Khadir SECK, à Rabat (Maroc)

items.title: NLC, TUC end rift, unite against anti-worker policies
items.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Nigeria’s two major labour centres, the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC), have resolved their differences and agreed to strengthen their cooperation following the intervention of former leaders of both organisations. The reconciliation, announced at a joint world press conference on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, marks an end to the public disagreement that had threatened unity within the organised labour movement. The peace deal was brokered by former presidents of the two labour centres, who intervened to resolve the dispute and restore harmonious working relations between their leaderships. In a joint statement signed by NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, and TUC President General, Comrade Festus Osifo, the organisations reaffirmed their commitment to unity, solidarity and the protection of Nigerian workers’ rights and welfare. The statement acknowledged that a misunderstanding between the two labour centres had played out in the public domain but said the intervention of their former leaders had successfully resolved the disagreement. “It is no longer news that a family misunderstanding arose between the two Labour Centers, which unfortunately played out in the public domain. However, in the true spirit of labour solidarity, maturity and collective responsibility, distinguished former presidents of NLC and TUC intervened and worked tirelessly to resolve the disagreements. “We are pleased to announce that their intervention has yielded the desired results, and the misunderstanding has been amicably resolved,” the statement said. The two organisations declared that the unity of Nigerian workers was more important than disagreements among their leaders, pledging to work together in the interest of workers, pensioners and other vulnerable groups. They said the challenges confronting Nigerian workers required solidarity rather than division, adding that their common struggle must not be undermined by institutional differences or leadership disagreements. Both centres also reaffirmed that workers’ welfare, dignity and material well-being remained non-negotiable, stressing that their renewed partnership would focus on confronting exploitation, defending decent work, demanding economic justice and resisting policies they consider detrimental to workers and pensioners. “We are determined to ensure that our differences do not provide an opportunity for anti-worker forces to weaken the labour movement or undermine the gains achieved through decades of collective struggle,” they said. To sustain the reconciliation, the labour centres said they had agreed to introduce measures to promote mutual respect, strengthen working relations, establish effective mechanisms for resolving future disagreements and prevent a recurrence of such disputes. They expressed appreciation to six former labour leaders whose intervention facilitated the peace agreement. Mediators They are Comrades Hassan Sunmonu, Peace Obiajulu, Peter Esele, Ayuba Wabba, Bobboi Bala Kaigama and Quadri Olaleye. The organisations described their intervention as a demonstration of the enduring values and shared sacrifices upon which the labour movement was built. They also called on their affiliates, state councils, industrial unions, workers and pensioners across the country to remain united and committed to the collective struggle. The statement urged workers not to allow the disagreement to erode their confidence in the two organisations, declaring that both centres remained united in their pursuit of social and economic justice. The joint statement was signed by Ajaero and Osifo, while Sunmonu signed on behalf of former presidents of the two labour centres. items.title: JAMB ends office visits for course changes
items.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has introduced a fully online process for candidates seeking to change their preferred institutions or courses, eliminating the need for physical visits to its offices to access the service. The new arrangement allows candidates to independently make the changes through the Board’s e-Facility portal from any location with internet access. The initiative is expected to reduce queues, transportation costs, waiting time and other inconveniences associated with physically accessing the service. In a statement issued by its Acting Director, Public Affairs and Protocol, Dr Fabian Benjamin, the Board said the development was part of efforts to improve service delivery and align its operations with the Federal Government’s Ease of Doing Business policy. Under the arrangement, candidates can complete the entire process, including payment, authentication and submission, online without visiting JAMB offices or accredited facilities. To access the service, candidates are required to log into the JAMB e-Facility portal at https://efacility.jamb.gov.ng using their registered email addresses and passwords. After logging in, they should select “Corrections and Uploads” from the sidebar menu, click on “Change of Programme/Institution”, select UTME and indicate the examination year for which the correction is required. Candidates are then expected to generate a payment invoice by clicking on “Make New Payment” and complete the transaction through the CREDO payment platform using a debit card or bank transfer. The Board advised candidates to return to the payment page on their profiles after making payment to confirm that the status has changed from “PENDING” to “PAID (Not Used)”. After confirming payment, candidates should return to the Change of Institution/Course page, enter their preferred institution and/or programme details and validate the transaction using a One-Time Password (OTP) sent to their registered email addresses. The process is completed by clicking the “SAVE” button, after which a confirmation message indicating that the change has been successfully made will be displayed. Candidates are also required to print their Change of Programme/Institution slips and log into the Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS) to confirm that their new choices have been updated. JAMB cautioned candidates to carefully review their selections before submitting requests to avoid errors. It also stressed that candidates must ensure their payment status reads “PAID (Not Used)” before proceeding and have access to their registered email accounts to receive and validate the OTP. The Board further advised candidates to carry out the process through their individual profiles rather than engage intermediaries or disclose their login details and OTPs to third parties. It said there was no need to pay individuals to perform a service candidates could complete independently online. According to the statement, the Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, reaffirmed the Board’s commitment to using technology to remove bureaucratic bottlenecks, improve service delivery and make essential services accessible to candidates irrespective of their locations. The Board said the objective was to enable candidates to spend less time dealing with administrative processes and more time pursuing their educational aspirations. The initiative is the latest in a series of measures aimed at reducing physical visits to JAMB offices, easing pressure on its facilities and improving service delivery to candidates and other stakeholders. items.title: Dixinn : après des décennies d’attente, le quartier Hafia réclame un collège public, la maire interpelle les autorités
items.description: La maire de la commune de Dixinn, Aïssata Soumah, a profité du lancement du programme « École propre, quartier exemplaire », ce lundi 16 novembre 2026, à l’école primaire Elhadj Oumar 1, à Hafia Château d’Eau, pour porter un plaidoyer en faveur de la construction du premier collège public de Hafia. Devant plusieurs membres du gouvernement, des responsables de l’éducation et des représentants de la communauté éducative, l’élue a attiré l’attention sur l’absence d’infrastructures publiques d’enseignement secondaire dans cette zone, une situation qu’elle affirme perdurer depuis des décennies. D’entrée, la maire a rappelé l’histoire de l’établissement qui accueillait la cérémonie, soulignant que sa création répondait déjà à une volonté des populations locales exprimée en 1962. Soixante-quatre ans après, elle estime que la question de la poursuite du parcours scolaire des enfants de Hafia demeure entière. Avant d’évoqué le poids démographique de Hafia, composé de huit quartiers et comptant, selon les chiffres qu’elle a avancés, plus de 80 000 habitants. « Mesdames et messieurs les ministres, permettez-moi de vous dire une vérité que Hafia porte depuis des décennies. Cette école, ce sont les habitants de Hafia qui l’ont voulue en 1962. 64 ans plus tard, ils attendent toujours la suite.Hafia, ce sont 8 quartiers, plus de 80 000 habitants, plus de 4 habitants de Dixinn sur 10 sont de Hafia. Et à Hafia, il n’y a pas un seul collège public. Jamais, jamais, jamais ! », a-t-elle martelé. Cette absence d’établissement secondaire public constitue, selon elle, un obstacle majeur pour les enfants qui terminent le cycle primaire. Une fois admis en 7e année, ces derniers sont contraints de poursuivre leur scolarité hors de leur quartier, avec les difficultés de déplacement et les charges financières que cela implique pour leurs familles. « Regardez ces enfants : le jour où ils réussiront leur entrée en 7ème, il n’y aura pas de collège public au bout de l’œuvre. Il faudra quitter le quartier, traverser les grands axes, payer un transport ou une école privée que tant de familles ne peuvent malheureusement pas payer. Alors, certains s’accrochent, d’autres abandonnent tout simplement. Et vous savez qui abandonne en premier ? Nos filles », a-t-elle interpellé. La maire a particulièrement insisté sur les conséquences de cette situation pour la scolarisation des jeunes filles. En prenant pour exemple la composition de l’école où se déroulait la cérémonie, elle a invité les autorités à mesurer le nombre d’élèves qui risquent de ne pas accéder au secondaire. « Dans notre pays, à peine plus d’une fille sur trois n’a jamais au collège y est inscrite. Ici, dans cette école, plus de la moitié des élèves sont des filles. Combien d’entre elles franchiront la porte d’un collège ? Combien d’entre elles?Aujourd’hui, nous apprenons à ces enfants à garder leur école propre. Une école propre, c’est une promesse, un collège, c’est un avenir » L’élue a présenté cette situation comme un oubli transmis d’une génération à une autre. Elle a ainsi appelé à une mobilisation collective pour corriger ce manque.«Je ne suis pas venue me plaindre, ce n’est la faute de personne ici présent. C’est un oubli que chaque génération a laissé à la suivante. Le réparer peut devenir notre fierté commune », a-t-elle précisé. Au-delà de ce constat, la maire de Dixinn a soumis trois propositions aux autorités afin de faire avancer le dossier. La première consiste à inscrire la construction du futur établissement dans les investissements de l’État dès 2027. « Alors, je vous fais trois propositions : Primo : inscrire le premier collège public de Hafia dans les investissements de l’État dès 2027 Secundo, madame la ministre : la commune de Dixinn est prête à rechercher le site avec l’État et à mobiliser famille et partenaires », a-t-elle affirmé. Tertio : fixer ensemble une date pour poser la première pierre du premier collège public de Hafia », a-t-elle insisté. S’adressant directement à la ministre de l’Éducation nationale, elle a également rappelé sa vision de l’éducation comme un parcours continu, de l’alphabétisation jusqu’à l’université. Elle estime que Hafia réclame simplement l’infrastructure qui lui permettra d’assurer la transition entre le primaire et les autres cycles d’enseignement. « Madame la ministre de l’Éducation nationale, vous voyez l’éducation comme un continuum de l’alphabétisation jusqu’à l’université. Hafia vous demande un seul maillon, celui qui manque entre l’école primaire et le reste de la vie », a-t-elle déclaré. Elle a notamment interpellé les personnalités présentes sur la nécessité de permettre aux enfants de Hafia de bénéficier des mêmes perspectives que ceux des autres quartiers.« Voilà, mesdames et messieurs les ministres, ce qui attend. Ils ne demandent pas la charité, ils demandent l’égalité des chances », a-t-elle lancé en désignant les parents d’élèves présents. Ajoutant « Madame la députée uninominale Mélia Soumah, entre vous et le dernier député de Hafia, il y a eu 5 générations. Sans collège à Hafia, il n’y aura pas une autre Mélia Soumah . Sans collège à Hafia, aucune Djenabou Touré ne viendra de Hafia pour occuper pour la première fois le poste de ministre de l’Administration du territoire et de la Décentralisation.Sans collège à Hafia, pas de Bintou Keïta originaire de Hafia pour porter haut le drapeau de la Guinée dans le Champ de Mars à Moscou ou au Kivu dans le Congo profond… pas de gouverneur de Conakry M’mahawa », a-t-elle poursuivi. Pour conclure, la maire a insisté sur la nécessité de dépasser les discours et de poser des actes concrets en faveur des générations futures. Elle estime que la construction de cet établissement constituerait un héritage dont les enfants se souviendront bien au-delà des promesses formulées aujourd’hui. « Le jour où Hafia aura son collège, ces enfants ne se souviendront pas de nos discours, ils se souviendront de la porte que nous leur aurons ouverte. Hafia veut dire la santé et la paix, donnons-leur aussi le savoir », a-t-elle conclu. À travers ce plaidoyer, Aïssata Soumah place ainsi la construction du premier collège public de Hafia parmi les attentes adressées aux autorités éducatives et gouvernementales. Mayi Cissé L’article Dixinn : après des décennies d’attente, le quartier Hafia réclame un collège public, la maire interpelle les autorités est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Ouganda : le fils de Museveni affiche ouvertement ses ambitions présidentielles
items.description: Le general Muhoozi Kainerugaba a affiche sans ambiguïte ses ambitions politiques. « Je serai candidat a la presidence de ce pays apres Mzee . Personne ne m'en empechera », a ecrit le chef des forces de defense ougandaises (UPDF) dans un message publie le 17 novembre sur X, avant de faire appel au soutien de Dieu et de ses compatriotes. La declaration survient apres une breve interruption de son activite sur le reseau social, durant laquelle son porte-parole militaire avait indique qu'il se preparait a une victoire politique en 2031. Le fils du president Yoweri Museveni, qui dirige l'Ouganda depuis 1986, avait exprime a plusieurs reprises son intention de briguer la magistrature supreme, ce qui fait de lui l'une des figures centrales du debat sur l'apres-Museveni. Son retour sur X s'est accompagne d'une serie de messages virulents, notamment a l'encontre de l'opposant Kizza Besigye. Muhoozi Kainerugaba a declare vouloir demander a son pere de renvoyer l'ancien candidat a la presidentielle en prison, estimant que les efforts entrepris pour parvenir a un dialogue avaient suffisamment dure. Il a aussi rejete toute perspective de negociation avec celui qu'il qualifie de « traître ». Le general s'en est pris aux medias, menacant de dix ans de prison les organes de presse qui, selon lui, denigreraient sa famille ou lui-meme. Il a par ailleurs annonce vouloir prochainement devoiler une nouvelle politique encadrant les activites des medias etrangers en Ouganda. Une succession de plus en plus ouvertement evoquee Ses declarations alimentent les speculations sur une possible transmission du pouvoir au sein de la famille Museveni. a la tete de l'armee et president de la Patriotic League of Uganda (PLU), une organisation qui soutient ses ambitions, Muhoozi Kainerugaba beneficie deja de l'appui de plusieurs personnalites politiques et de partisans qui militent en faveur de sa candidature. L'hypothese d'une succession en 2031 est regulierement avancee, alors que Yoweri Museveni vient de prolonger son regne a l'issue de l'election presidentielle de janvier 2026. Le chef de l'etat n'a toutefois pas officiellement designe son fils comme successeur, ni annonce ses intentions concernant la prochaine echeance electorale. La perspective d'une devolution dynastique suscite des interrogations sur l'avenir du pays, notamment sur le role de l'armee dans la vie politique et les conditions d'une eventuelle transition.
